October 22, 1941.

Assassination of a Japanese Subject.

At 7.30 a.m. October 21, Mr. Iwakura, a
Vide Sp. Br. Japanese employee of the Nantao Office of the Central
Report dated China Water & Electricity Company (Japanese) was shot
21/10/41. by desperadoes in front of the Company's quarters, at
No. 19 Mong Hwa Ka (夢花街), near Vung Miao Road,
City. The victim sustaining a bullet wound in his
abdomen and was immediately removed to the Foo Ming
Hospital where he was pronounced dead on arrival.

As the assassins are still at large, the
Japanese Gendarmerie in Nantao have issued a circular
notice offering a reward of $2,000 for the arrest of
the assassins.

W. 22/10 Jol

1941年10月22日。

一名日本臣民被刺杀。

10月21日上午7时30分，华中水电公司（日资）南市办事处的一名日本雇员岩仓（Iwakura，音译）先生，在市内文庙路附近的梦花街19号该公司宿舍前，被暴徒枪击。详见1941年10月21日的特务科报告。受害者腹部中弹，随即被送往福明医院，抵达时被宣布死亡。

由于刺客仍在逃，驻南市的日本宪兵队发布通缉令，悬赏2,000元缉拿刺客。

October 21, 1941.

Attempted Assassination of a Japanese Subject
in Nantao.

According to information received, a Japanese
subject was shot and wounded by desperadoes on Vung
Miao Road (文廟路), City, at about 7 o'clock this
morning (October 21). All the iron gates leading to
Nantao along Boulevard des Deux Republiques were
subsequently closed at 9 a.m. to-day. At 10 a.m. even
date the barricades were re-opened, the closure having
lasted for one hour.

1941年10月21日。

南市一名日本臣民遇刺未遂。

据收到的消息，今天（10月21日）早上7点左右，一名日本臣民在市内文庙路被暴徒枪击受伤。随后，沿共和大道（Boulevard des Deux Republiques）通往南市的所有铁门于今天上午9时关闭。同日（当天）上午10时，路障重新开放，封闭持续了一小时。

October 10, 1941.

Attempted Assassination of
a Japanese soldier in Nantao.

At 4.20 p.m., October 9, 1941, a Japanese
soldier was shot by a male person when he was
directing three road workers placing barbed wire
barricades on Lee Moo Loo, Nantao. He was
seriously wounded by the leg and abdomen. A
stray bullet hurt one of the workers also.

（印：FILE 11. 10. 41）

At about 5.30 p.m. the same day, the
Japanese military in cooperation with the French
Police closed all the gates and carried out a
thorough search in the district.

The gates along Min Kuo Road were still
closed this morning. No persons are allowed
to pass the gates except officials connected
with the Japanese sides.

（批：6/10/41 ... 41 10 M）

1941年10月10日。

南市一名日本士兵遇刺未遂。

1941年10月9日下午4时20分，一名日本士兵在南市李慕路（Lee Moo Loo，音译）指挥三名道路工人设置铁丝网路障时，被一名男子枪击。其腿部和腹部受重伤。一颗流弹也伤及其中一名工人。

（印：档案 1941年10月11日）

当天下午5时30分左右，日军与法国警察合作，关闭了该地区的所有大门，并进行了彻底搜查。

民国路沿线的大门今晨仍然关闭。除与日方有关的官员外，任何人不得通过大门。

August 11, 1941. 8 //

Raid on 794 Loh Ka Pang Road, Nantao

During the afternoon of August 4, 1941, a
party of five members under the charge of TAO SIH SUNG,
Chief of the Shanghai Office of the Provisionally
Organized 13th Division of the Nanking Government Army,
9 West End Gardens, off Yu Yuen Road, conducted a raid
at 794 Loh Ka Pang Road, Nantao. This address was
given as the Shanghai Office of the 13th Division, but
no such office was found on the premises, nor were any
responsible persons present. There are three
bungalows at this place, and two signboards of the
ZEU FOONG BAN KEE Sand and Pebble Hong (瑞豐盤記砂石行)
and the ZEU FOONG BAN KEE Transportation Hong
(瑞豐盤記汽車運輸行) were found outside the houses.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / AUG 11 1941 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

突袭南市罗家浜路794号

1941年8月4日下午，由南京政府军暂编第十三师上海办事处主任陶思松（TAO SIH SUNG，音译）率领的五人小组，对南市罗家浜路794号进行了突袭。陶思松的办公地点位于愚园路9号西园弄。该地址被列为第十三师上海办事处，但在现场未发现此类办事处，也无任何负责人在场。该处有三座平房，屋外发现两块招牌，分别为“瑞豐盤記砂石行”和“瑞豐盤記汽車運輸行”。

August 8, 1941 8 41

Iron Gates on Nantao-French Concession Borders

On the morning of August 8, the iron gates on the
South End of Boulevard de Montigny and Rue Chateau d'Eau
were reopened. The other iron gates on the Nantao-
French Concession borders, however, remain close, as searches
are still being conducted in the refugee zone of Nantao
by City Government policemen.

At noon on August 7, the following notice issued
by Col. Loo Ying, Chief of the Police Bureau of the
Shanghai Special Municipality, was posted on the various
thoroughfares in Nantao :-

"Owing to the occurrence of an unfortunate
incident in the city district, the authorities
have been compelled to close the iron gates for a
number of days, thus causing certain inconvenience
to the residents of Nantao. However, the residents
should also shoulder some responsibility. If
persons are observed acting in a suspicious manner,
the residents should immediately report to the
police bureau so that investigations may be carried
out and recurrence of unfortunate incidents prevented.
Should any such unfortunate incident take place
again, the iron gates will likely be closed for a
long period. It is therefore hoped that assistance
will be rendered by the residents."

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 8 AUG. 1941）

1941年8月8日 8 41

南市-法租界边界的铁门

8月8日上午，蒙梯尼大道（Boulevard de Montigny）南端和城堡水路（Rue Chateau d'Eau）的铁门重新开放。然而，南市-法租界边界上的其他铁门仍然关闭，因为市政府警察仍在南市难民区进行搜查。

8月7日中午，上海市警察局局长陆英（Loo Ying，音译）上校发布的以下告示张贴在南市各主要街道上：-

“因市区发生不幸事件，当局被迫关闭铁门数日，给南市居民带来一定不便。然而，居民也应承担部分责任。若发现有人行为可疑，居民应立即向警察局报告，以便进行调查并防止不幸事件再次发生。若再次发生此类不幸事件，铁门可能会长期关闭。因此，希望居民予以协助。”

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1941年8月8日）

August 7, 1941.
Iron Gates on Nantao-French Concession Borders Reopened

The iron gates on the Nantao-French Concession
borders which were closed during the night of July 31
immediately after the shooting and wounding of a certain
male Chinese and a Japanese Gendarme were reopened at
1 p.m. August 7. Since then, the communications between
the French Concession and Nantao have been restored to
normal.

（批：W 7/8）

南市-法租界边界的铁门重新开放

7月31日晚，在一名中国男子和一名日本宪兵被枪击受伤后，南市-法租界边界上关闭的铁门于8月7日下午1时重新开放。此后，法租界与南市之间的交通已恢复正常。

June 12, 1941.

Arrests in French Concession

At 10.45 a.m., June 11, members of the
French Police and the Japanese Gendarmerie arrested
6 male and three female Chinese at the Dah Hwa
( 大 華 ) Tailors Shop, No. 176 Boulevard de
Montigny.

Two male and one female Chinese were
subsequently released whilst the remaining six
persons were handed over to the Japanese authorities.

It is reported that the arrests were made in
connection with assassination of a Japanese Gendarme
in Nantso on May 24, 1941.

1941年6月12日。

法租界逮捕行动

6月11日上午10时45分，法国警察和日本宪兵队在蒙梯尼大道176号大华裁缝店逮捕了6名中国男性和3名中国女性。

随后，2名中国男性和1名中国女性被释放，其余6人被移交给日本当局。

据报道，此次逮捕与1941年5月24日在南素（Nantso，原文如此，应为南市 Nantao）刺杀一名日本宪兵的案件有关。

page_data.en:
June 9, 1941. 815513 (C)

Explosion of a Sulphuric Bomb in Nantao

At about 6.45 p.m. June 7, a sulphuric bomb was thrown by some unknown person at the rear entrance of house No. 2, Lane 64, Jiu Chong Ka (舊倉街), Nantao. The bomb exploded but nobody was injured.

Precautionary measures were immediately adopted in the vicinity by the Japanese Gendarmerie and the City Government Police. Traffic was held up and searches were conducted. It is learned that five suspects were arrested. In addition, the Japanese closed all the iron gates on the border of French Concession and Nantao with the result that some 4,000 to 5,000 people were prevented from entering the district. At 9 p.m. the iron gate on Rue Chateau d'Eau was allowed to be opened by the Japanese.

About 15 minutes after the bombing, the rifle of one of the City Government Policemen, who were adopting precautions in the vicinity, accidentally discharged wounding a woman and two children, all residing at No. 1 Shi Shen Li (希善里), Van Sung Road (萬生路), Nantao. They were removed to Tse Shen Hospital (慈善医院) at Kiu Miao Dee for treatment.

At 5 a.m. June 8, all the iron gates were re-opened and all the opium smoking and gambling dens in Nantao are now doing business as usual.

1941年6月9日。 815513 (C)

南市硫酸炸弹爆炸事件

6月7日下午6时45分左右，不明身份者在南市旧仓街64弄2号房屋的后门投掷了一枚硫酸炸弹。炸弹爆炸，但无人受伤。

日本宪兵队和市政府警察立即在该地区采取了预防措施。交通受阻，并进行了搜查。据悉，有五名嫌疑人被捕。此外，日本人关闭了法租界与南市边界上的所有铁门，导致约4,000至5,000人无法进入该地区。晚上9时，日本人允许打开城堡水路（Rue Chateau d'Eau）的铁门。

爆炸发生后约15分钟，一名在该地区采取预防措施的市政府警察的步枪意外走火，打伤了一名妇女和两名儿童，他们均居住在南市万生路希善里1号。他们被送往九亩地慈善医院接受治疗。

6月8日凌晨5时，所有铁门重新开放，南市所有的鸦片烟馆和赌档现已照常营业。

May 27, 1941.

Situation in Nantao following the assassination of a
Japanese Gendarme on May 24.

Following the assassination of a Japanese
Gendarme in Nantao on May 24, the Japanese authorities
made thorough searches in the district but without
result. All ricksha coolies in the area, together with
their vehicles, were detained by the Japanese authorities
at Boon Lai Sz Lane, Small West Gate, because, it is
reported, the assassin or assassins made good their escape
by riding in rickshas. The coolies are still under
detention pending investigations.

The iron gates on the borders between French
Concession and Nantao, which were closed by the Japanese
authorities immediately following the assassination, were
re-opened this morning, May 27, and the gambling dens there
which suspended business after the shooting, resumed
operating to-day.

Commandant of Police
Sir
Inf
J. Sharman
A. C. (Sp. Br.)

1941年5月27日。

5月24日一名日本宪兵被刺杀后的南市局势。

继5月24日一名日本宪兵在南市被刺杀后，日本当局在该地区进行了彻底搜查，但未有结果。该地区的所有黄包车夫及其车辆均被日本当局扣留在小西门奔来寺弄（Boon Lai Sz Lane，音译），因为据报刺客乘坐黄包车逃脱。车夫们仍在拘留中，等待调查。

法租界与南市边界上的铁门在刺杀发生后立即被日本当局关闭，已于今晨（5月27日）重新开放，枪击后停止营业的赌档也于今日恢复运营。

Assassination of a Japanese Gendarme
in Nantao.
--------------------------

April 23, 1941.

Escape of prisoners from custody of Japanese
Gendarmerie (Nantao).

At about 8 a.m., April 22, 1941, following
the escape from their cells of 15 prisoners, who were
in custody for theft of electric wires or as political
suspects, the Japanese Gendarmerie stationed at Boong
Lai Road, Nantao, immediately intensified the search
of pedestrians at the various iron gates and no
persons are now allowed to leave Nantao without
"citizens certificates". This restriction, however,
does not apply to persons entering the area.
Closure of the iron gates and the alleged shooting
of Japanese as reported in the newspapers is
incorrect.

page_data.en:
Japanese Search For
Escaped Terrorists

Nantao Closed As Nine Alleged Chungking
Terrorists Break Prison; Five Agents
Executed In Western District

The Japanese Gendarmerie and Nanking controlled City
Government Police Forces at Nantao were still searching to-
day for the nine alleged Chungking terrorists who made good
their escape from a Nantao prison yesterday, the Evening
Post learned from reliable sources today.

Following the prison break early
yesterday morning, an intensive
search throughout Nantao City
was carried out by the joint
forces of the Japanese Gen-
darmerie and Chinese constables of
the City Government Police there.
All gates, except one from the
French Concession leading to
Nantao were closed by the French,
Municipal Police in a measure to
aid their search.

Results Unknown

The results of the intensified
search were not disclosed today
by either the Japanese authori-
ties in Nantao, but usually well
informed quarters said that all
the nine alleged Chungking ter-
rorists were still at large.

All persons trying to enter
Nantao today were subjected to
a severe search along the gates
by Chinese constables of the City
Government Police Force, it was
learned.

Murder Rumored

Earlier reports said that a
Korean was shot somewhere in
Nantao and the intensified search
was the result of this murder, it
will be recalled. This alleged mur-
der could not be confirmed from
responsible quarters this morning.

All the nine escaped Chungking
terrorists were arrested two weeks
ago in different places in Nantao
and the Western areas of Shang-
hai, it was said.

Execution Carried Out

Meanwhile another public exe-
cution was witnessed by many
Chinese residents along Chung
San Road, off Brenan Road, as
five Chungking agents were exe-
cuted by the Political Police
Bureau of the Nanking Regime
late yesterday afternoon.

The five alleged Chungking
terrorists were executed on charge
of the Nanking promulgated
Martial Laws, it was reported by
the Nanking sponsored papers this
morning.

Blue Shirt Men

Among the five persons were
two members of the Blue Shirts,
generally regarded as Chungking's
secret service organization, it was
said.

The chief of the Intelligence
Department of Chungking's
Special Activities Bureau in
Shanghai, Li Sze-ping, was also
executed the papers said.
page_data.zh:
日本搜捕
逃脱的恐怖分子

南市封锁，九名所谓重庆恐怖分子越狱；五名特工在西区被处决

据《晚报》今日从可靠消息来源获悉，驻南市的日本宪兵队和南京控制的市政府警察部队今日仍在搜捕昨天从南市监狱成功逃脱的九名所谓重庆恐怖分子。

继昨天清晨发生越狱事件后，日本宪兵队和当地市政府警察的中国警员联合部队在南市全城进行了密集搜查。除一扇从法租界通往南市的门外，所有大门均由法租界和公共租界警察关闭，以协助搜查。

结果未知

日本当局今日未披露强化搜查的结果，但通常消息灵通人士称，这九名所谓的重庆恐怖分子仍在逃。

据悉，今日所有试图进入南市的人员在各关口均受到市政府警察部队中国警员的严厉搜查。

谋杀传闻

早先的报道曾称，一名朝鲜人在南市某处被枪杀，而强化搜查是此次谋杀的结果。今晨未能从负责部门证实这一所谓的谋杀案。

据说，这九名逃脱的重庆恐怖分子是两周前在南市和上海西区不同地点被捕的。

执行处决

与此同时，许多中国居民在勃伦纳路（Brenan Road）旁的中山路目睹了另一次公开处决，五名重庆特工于昨天下午晚些时候被南京政权的政治警察局处决。

据南京支持的报纸今晨报道，这五名所谓的重庆恐怖分子因违反南京颁布的戒严令而被处决。

蓝衣社成员

据说，在这五人中有两名蓝衣社成员，该组织通常被视为重庆的情报机构。

报纸称，重庆特种活动局上海情报处处长李士平（Li Sze-ping，音译）也被处决。

Subject "Nantao Merchants Friendly Association" - new body formed.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih. Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum.

A new organization known as the "Nantao
Merchants Friendly Association" (滬南區商業聯誼會)
was recently organized by some 200 shop owners in
Nantao, with offices at 232 Loo Shiang Yuan Road,
Nantao. The association was formally inaugurated
at a meeting held in the Van Tsoh (萬竹) Primary
School, 243 Loo Shiang Yuan Road, Nantao, on February
23, 1941, when the following resolutions were passed :
1. that member shops pay a monthly membership fee of
$2.00 each towards the upkeep of the association.
2. That the association assist member shops in
solving disputes arising out of their business
or from other reasons.
An executive committee of 12 persons was elected,
including the following :
1. Chu Chih Tsieu (居季秋) - aged 35, native
of Shanghai, Manager of Nan Dah (南大) Cigarette
and Money Exchange Shop, 13 Dah Ching Road.
2. Dzien Tsien Chung (錢鈞濟) - aged 41, native
of Woosung, clerk employed by a lawyer.
3. Moh Loh Cheu (馬六舟) - aged 39, a native
of Chingkiang, owner of Zung Dah Soy Shop, 13 Dah
Ching Road.

Subject Nantao Situation - ruined premises and population.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien Pih Forwarded by C.J.I. Tabrum

The Nantao Administrative Office of the
Shanghai City Government, on November 20, 1940, issued a
proclamation instructing the owners of property in
Nantao to commence repairs of their ruined premises
within two months, failing which the Administrative
Office would repair the property and convert same to
their own use for a period of three years. As most
of the property owners paid no attention to the
instruction, the Nantao Administrative Office issued
a second proclamation on February 13, to the effect,
that the property owners must comply with the order
before the end of February or the Administrative Office
would take the step indicated in the first proclama-
tion.

The population in Nantao was 183,644 persons
at the end of 1940.

City Government Police Bureau orders suppression of
activities by idlers in Nantao.

With reference to the attached translation
dated February 7, 1941 to the effect that City Govern-
ment Police Bureau has ordered the suppression of
activities by idlers in Nantao, enquiries show that
all Police stations in Nantao have received, on February
5, the following instructions from Commissioner Loo
Ying of the City Government Police Bureau.
"In order to maintain good peace and order
in Nantao and to curb bad elements from disturbing
shops and residences, all illegal activities should
be strictly prohibited".
No proclamations have as yet been issued for
public information.
Opium hongs, gambling dens and other forms of
vice are still prevalent in the Nantao area.

February 10, 1941.

Pro-Japanese Propaganda in Nantao.

Pro-Japanese handbills purporting to emanate
from the Propaganda Department of the Nanking Government
were found posted in various parts of Nantao on
February 6. Specimen copies are unavailable.
Copies of a cartoon of an Anti-Foreign and
pro-Japanese nature were also posted in Nantao on
February 6. A specimen copy is attached.
This cartoon contains three pictures, a description
of which is given below:
(a) Heading : "Peoples of the same race are fighting
while others are getting the benefit."
The picture shows a British and an American
partaking of food left on a table by two Japanese and two
Chinese who are exchanging blows :
(b) Heading : "Corporation will lead to mutual prosperity".
The picture under this heading shows two Chinese
and two Japanese shaking hands by the side of the table
with food while the British and the American are in the
act of fleeing.
(c) Heading : "The scorched earth policy will lead
the nation to extinction while peace
and cooperation will bring about national
prosperity."
The picture under this heading shows several
Chinese in the war of resistance, digging trenches in
the design of two Chinese characters "National Extinction."
It also shows a Japanese and a Chinese proceeding together
along the "highway of peace."

画面显示一名英国人和一名美国人正在享用留在桌上的食物，而两名日本人和两名中国人正在互相殴打：
(b) 标题：“合作导致共同繁荣”。
该标题下的画面显示两名中国人和两名日本人在摆满食物的桌旁握手，而英国人和美国人正在逃离。
(c) 标题：“焦土政策导致国家灭亡，和平合作带来国家繁荣。”
该标题下的画面显示几名抗战中的中国人正在挖掘战壕，战壕形状构成“亡国”两个汉字。画面还显示一名日本人和一名中国人正沿着“和平大道”共同前进。

On the instructions of the Bureau of Social
Affairs, Shanghai City Government, the Nantao District
Administrative Office, 50 Ih Soh Ka, Boon Lei Road,
Nantao, are conducting a winter relief to the poor
in the Nantao District which will last for ten days,
commencing from January 27, 1941. Those who can
prove that they are bona fide but poor residents

certificates, can apply to the Administrative Office

January 22, 1941.
Usurious pawnshops in Nantao and Western District
----------
With reference to the attached article from the
January 13th issue of the Evening Echo on the subject
"Usurious pawnshops ordered closed by local Government
Bureau", enquiries have been made with the following result:-
On January 17, twenty-three of some 80 pawnshops
located in the Old West Gate area in Nantao received a
circular notice from the Bureau of Social Affairs, through
the Nantao Administrative Office( 50 Ih Soh Ka, Boon Lai
Road, Nantao), instructing them to close their businesses
by the end of the current month because of the usurious
interest charged and limiting the term of loans to one month.
The order further requires the pawnshops to allow the pledgers
to redeem their property within six months from the date of
closure at a monthly interest of 3%.
The Bureau of Social Affairs, however, has not yet
taken any action against the many "open air pawnshops"
(stalls) operating on open spaces near the gambling dens in
Nantao and the Western District, O.O.L. These "pawnshops"
charge an interest of 30% for ten days, and confiscate the
articles pledged if they are not redeemed within that period.
The pawn receipts can also be pawned at the same rate of
interest. The owners of such "pawnshops", which are
patronized by gamblers only, are loafers mostly having
connections with the Japanese Gendarmerie stationed in the
districts concerned . It will be difficult for the Shanghai
City Government to suppress them in view of the fact that
the gambling dens in Nantao are still operating despite
Mayor Chen Kung Po's order for their suppression.

（批：Original filed J 8155）
（右上角手写注记：8155 A (?) / 27 / 11）
page_data.zh:
1941年1月22日。
南市及西区的高利贷当铺
----------
关于附上的1月13日《晚声报》上题为“地方政府局下令关闭高利贷当铺”的文章，经查询，结果如下：
1月17日，位于南市老西门地区的约80家当铺中的23家，通过南市行政公署（南市蓬莱路50号）收到社会局的通函通知，指令其因收取高利贷利息并将贷款期限限制为一个月，须在本月底前停止营业。该命令还要求当铺允许典当人在停业之日起六个月内赎回其财产，月息为3%。
然而，社会局尚未对在南市和西区（O.O.L.）赌场附近的空地上经营的许多“露天当铺”（摊位）采取任何行动。这些“当铺”收取十天30%的利息，如果物品在此期间未被赎回，则予以没收。当票也可以以相同的利率再次典当。这类仅受赌徒光顾的“当铺”的主人大多是闲散人员，主要与驻扎在相关地区的日本宪兵队有联系。鉴于尽管陈公博市长下令取缔，南市的赌场仍在运营，上海市政府将难以取缔这些当铺。

（批注：原件归档于 J 8155）
（右上角手写注记：8155 A (?) / 27 / 11）

Subject Nantao - registration of shops and factories.
Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Following the issue, on March 12, 1940, of
a joint notice by the Nantao Administrative Office and
the Nantao Section of the Japanese Military Special
Service Department, requiring shops and factories in
Nantao, to register with the Nantao Administrative
Office, only about 20 shops have applied for registration,
while the others are adopting a wait-and-see attitude in
view of the formation of the new Central Government.

Persons applying for registration of their
shops must produce citizen's certificates and fill in
application forms, a copy of which is attached hereto
together with translation. The Nantao Administrative
Office will conduct investigations as regards the
applications received and will issue registration
certificates after completion of investigations.

Application forms are issued free but
registration fees, the rate of which has not been decided
upon, will be collected.

REPORT
Date October 8, 1940.

Subject Public ricsha coolies in Nantao on strike

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

(批：R.J. Yorke)

On the morning of October 7, 1940, some
9,000 public ricsha coolies in Nantao declared
a strike to protest against the recent increase
of 10 cents in the rates for renting which was
announced by the owners as effective from October
1, 1940.

The daily rental for public ricshas was
formerly 50 cents and the recent increase of 10
cents, it is learned, is because all public ricsha
owners have been recently compelled to join the
Nantao Public Ricsha Owners' Association (南市人力
車業同業公會), No.60 Ying Hsuen Road, Small West
Gate, Nantao, which was reorganized from the former
Nantao Ricsha Corporation (南市人力車公司組合).
The members of the association are required to
pay a monthly membership fee of $4.00 towards the
upkeep of the association which has several
Japanese subjects as executives.

There were 8,000 public ricshas in operation
in Nantao but following the strike only 500 public
ricshas were on the streets, which are being pulled
by their respective owners.

Pan Lien Pih

Subject Nantao Ricsha Corporation - formation

Made by D. I. Fan Lien Fih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

A new organisation known as the "Nantao
Ricsha Corporation (南市人力車公司組織)" came into
existence during the early part of June, 1940 with
offices at 65 Ning Shiung Road (寧勳路), Small
West Gate, Nantao.

The corporation was formed, with the object
of creating a monopoly, by YU DA CHING (于達清),
with the sanction of the Japanese Consulate and the
Japanese Military Authorities stationed in Nantao.
Yu was a Standing Committee member of the now
defunct "Nantao Ricsha Owners' Association"
which operated in 1937 and owns 100 ricshas.

A notice instructing all ricsha owners in
the district to join this corporation by June 15,
1940, has been posted outside the office. On
joining the corporation, the ricsha owner has to
pay 50 cents for a puller's badge, bearing a number
the same as that of the licence of the ricsha and
another $2 for a jacket to be worn by the puller.

The corporation has now announced that an
increase, effective from June 16, 1940, will be
enforced for the ricsha hire charges from 40 cents to
60 cents per ricsha per day. 10 cents of the
increase which amounts to 20 cents, must be paid to
the corporation while the remaining 10 cents will be
retained by the owner.

一个名为“南市人力车公司组织 (Nantao Ricsha Corporation)”的新机构于1940年6月上旬成立，办公地点位于南市小西门宁勋路 (Ning Shiung Road) 65号。

该公司由于达清 (YU DA CHING) 在日本驻沪领事馆及驻南市日本军当局的批准下组建，旨在建立垄断。于是氏曾是1937年运作的现已解散的“南市人力车主协会”的常务委员，拥有100辆人力车。

一则通知已张贴于办公室外，指示该地区所有人力车主须于1940年6月15日前加入该公司。加入该公司时，车主需支付50美分购买一枚拉车夫徽章，其号码与人力车执照号码相同，另需支付2美元购买一件供拉车夫穿着的外套。

该公司现已宣布，自1940年6月16日起，每辆人力车每日租金将从40美分涨至60美分。增加的20美分中，10美分须上缴该公司，其余10美分由车主保留。

Subject The Nantao Citizens' Federation - Formed.

Made by D. I. Fan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With a view to instituting pro-Wang Ching
Wei activities in Nantao, Ting Muh Tsung
(丁默村), Minister of Social Affairs of
the New Central Government, nominated about the
middle part of May, 1940, Kung Kia Kyi (耿嘉基),
Secretary of the former Shanghai City Government,
Wang Mei-Yung (汪曼雲), Vice-Chief of the
Bureau of Social Affairs of the Orthodox Kuomintang,
and Oo Shou Gee (胡寿祺), a staff member of
the former Bureau of Social Affairs, to the task
of forming a "Nantao Citizens' Federation" which
will be responsible for the rehabilitation of
Nantao. The Federation was formally inaugurated
on May 28, 1940 at No. 129 Zang Vung Road (尚文路),
Nantao, and has a staff at present of some 20
employees who are under the supervision of Oo Shou
Gee. This person is making efforts to bring the
following projects into effect immediately.

1. Enlistment of members for the Federation.
2. The lighting of streets and streets
cleaning.
3. To prolong the opening hours for the
iron gates between the French Concession
and Nantao.
4. Organization of a "Merchants Volunteer
Corps".
5. Mediation in rent disputes.
6. The opening of "Hwo Wei" lotteries be
prohibited and cheap sale of daily
necessities be promoted.

With reference to Special Branch report on
the above dated June 15, 1939 and letter from H.B.M.
Consul-General to the Commissioner of Police, dated
June 26, 1939, requesting information regarding what
steps, if any, the French authorities are taking in
the matter, a copy of the initial French Police
report on the incident, together with translation is
attached hereto, from which it will be seen that the
incident was of a less serious nature than would
appear from the information obtained by the Special
Branch.

According to information obtained at French
Police Headquarters, on June 28, 1939, Mr. LADROITTE,
Manager of Cie Fse de Tramways, which Company is also
owner of the French Water Works, was informed of the
incident but did not take a serious view of the matter
merely suggesting that the Japanese authorities should
be informed that they should obtain permission from
the Company before visiting the Water Works. Two
passes, one to the Japanese Naval Landing Party and
one to the Japanese Gendarmerie, have since been issued
by the Company, authorizing visits by the Japanese
authorities.

According to the French Police, the purpose of
the Japanese visit was in order to ascertain if there
were any French marines posted in the Water Works but
no French details were present.

The French Water Works are situated in Nantao
about one mile from the boundary of the French Conces-
sion but owing to traffic restrictions in force in
Nantao, a detour has to be made in order to reach the
Water Works which makes the journey one of slightly
more than two miles. Officials of the French Water
Works are permitted to travel without interference
between the Concession and the Water Works. With
the exception of 2,000,000 galls. of water per day
which the Shanghai Water Works Co. has been supplying
to the French Concession since over five years, the
French Water Works is responsible for the whole of
the French Concession supply, exclusive of that
supplied by artesian wells. The main connection from
the Settlement is located at Hart Road and Avenue
Foch intersection. In addition to the main connection
there are eight connections located along Avenue Foch
and Avenue Edward VII, which can be used to supply
water from the Settlement to the French Concession
or vice versa in case of an emergency, but in such an
event the supply would have to be restricted to that
required by absolute necessity.
The French Water Works have no protection other
than that afforded by the presence of a French gunboat
which is usually berthed alongside the Kiousin Dock
which adjoins the French Water Works.

page_data.en:
Translation of French Police Report No.4132/S dated 13-6-39

At 2 p.m., June 11, two unarmed Japanese soldiers
presented themselves at the Nantao Waterworks of the
French Tramway Company (Avenue de Bezaure, Nantao), with
the object of inspecting the premises. As they were in
possession of no documents, they were refused admittance
by the foreign employee on duty. The two soldiers
withdrew but returned an hour later accompanied by an
officer who insisted on inspecting the works.

The foreigner on duty finally gave way. The
officer withdrew after the visit which lasted about
half-an-hour, stating that he was satisfied there were
no more French marines on the premises.

During the course of a conversation with
Mr. LADROITTE, of the French Tramways, the latter
informed me that the Company was not opposed in
principle to these visits, but that it would be
preferable if the Japanese officers proceeding to
the Works carried a permit which the Company is
quite ready to issue. S.I. YANKOVSKY will
approach the Japanese Military Authorities in Nantao
to learn to whom the written permit should be given.
page_data.zh:
1939年6月13日法国警方报告第4132/S号译文

6月11日下午2时，两名未携带武器的日本士兵来到位于南市贝扎尔路（Avenue de Bezaure）的法国电车公司南水电厂，意图视察厂区。由于他们没有任何证件，值班的外籍雇员拒绝其进入。两名士兵随即离开，但一小时后在一位军官的陪同下返回，该军官坚持要视察水厂。

值班的外籍人员最终让步。视察持续了约半小时，结束后该军官离开，并表示他已确认厂区内不再有法国海军陆战队。

在与法国电车公司的拉德罗伊特（LADROITTE）先生交谈过程中，后者告知我，公司在原则上并不反对这些访问，但如果前往水厂的日本军官持有公司乐意签发的许可证，则更为妥当。副督察员扬科夫斯基（YANKOVSKY）将接触南市日本军事当局，以确认证明书应开具给谁。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
                                S.1, Special Branch. Station xxxxx
            CONFIDENTIAL      REPORT              Date......June 15, 19 39.

Subject......French Water Works on Ki Tchan Ka, Nantao - visited by the...
             Japanese.
Made by.................................... Forwarded by ....................................

It is reported that at about 2.30 p.m. on June
11, 1939, a junior officer of the Japanese Military
together with a private called at the French Water
Works on Ki Tchan Ka, Nantao and requested permission
to enter the premises. They were told by a
French employee of the Company that no admission
was permitted to outsiders and that a signboard in
Chinese and Japanese to this effect was displayed
outside the main entrance of the Company, whereupon
they left. About an hour later, a Japanese
military truck arrived with more than twenty Japanese
soldiers under two officers who were fully armed
and carried two machine guns. The party alighted
and immediately forced an entry into the premises
of the Water Works. They remained on the
premises for about three quarters of an hour, visiting
the various departments of the Water Works and then
departed without incident.

In consequence of this forcible visit by the
Japanese Military, a rumour is in circulation in the
City to the effect that the water supply for the
French Concession will be cut off should an emergency
arise in the Foreign controlled areas.

Certified true copy.
M. C. Sandley

据报，1939年6月11日下午约2时30分，一名日本军方低级军官偕同一名列兵来到南市机厂街的法国水厂，请求允许进入厂区。公司的一名法国雇员告诉他们，外人不得入内，且在公司大门外已悬挂中英文及日文告示牌明示此规定，随后他们离开。约一小时后，一辆日本军用卡车抵达，车上载有二十多名日本士兵，由两名军官率领，全副武装并携带两挺机枪。这群人下车后立即强行闯入水厂厂区。他们在厂区内停留了约三刻钟，视察了水厂的各个部门，然后未发生冲突便离开。

由于日本军方的这次强行访问，市内流传一种谣言，称一旦外国控制区发生紧急情况，法租界的供水将被切断。

核证无误副本。
M. C. 桑德利（M. C. Sandley）

S. B. REGISTRY
January 22, 1941 D.

1st Company of the Asia Rehabilitation and
National Reconstruction Army

Some 100 soldiers under the command of
Chen Zung ( 陳丞 ) of the 1st Company of the Asia
Rehabilitation and National Reconstruction Army,
No.19, Lee Yen Ko Ka, Nantao, have recently been
disbanded by the Japanese Military Authorities.

The cause of the disbandment of Chen's
army, it is reported, is due to the fact that
Chen has been in contact with Zee Hoong Fah
( 徐鴻發 ), an ex-guerilla leader who operated
in Pootung and who surrendered to the Japanese
during 1939. In December, 1940, Zee Hoong Fah's
men committed several robberies in Pootung, which
became known to the Japanese Military Authorities
who immediately sent four Japanese officials and
a Chinese interpreter to make investigations
among Zee Hoong Fah's detachment.

Upon their arrival, two of the Japanese
officials and the Chinese interpreter were killed
by Zee's subordinates. This action on the part
of Zee's men aroused the anger of the Japanese
authorities, who immediately despatched soldiers
to arrest Zee Hoong Fah and his men, but they
scattered and are in hiding in Pootung.

Zee Hoong Fah approached Koo Yu Sung
( 顧裕聲 ) who was formerly an interpreter in the
employ of the Japanese Special Service, to bribe
Chen Zung with $40,000 if Chen Zung would recommend
Zee for the post of Vice Commander of the 1st
Company of the Asia Rehabilitation and National

（批：Original in D 8945）

秘密
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特务科登记处
1941年1月22日 D.

亚洲复兴救国军第一连

近期，驻扎在南市李延阁街（Lee Yen Ko Ka）19号的亚洲复兴救国军第一连连长陈丞（Chen Zung）麾下约100名士兵被日本军方当局解散。

据报，陈部被解散的原因在于陈丞曾与徐鸿发（Zee Hoong Fah）接触。徐鸿发系前游击队首领，曾在浦东活动，并于1939年间向日军投降。1940年12月，徐鸿发的手下在浦东实施数起抢劫案，此事为日本军方当局获悉，当局随即派遣四名日本官员及一名中文翻译前往徐鸿发分队进行调查。

日军抵达后，两名日本官员及中文翻译被徐的部下杀害。徐部此举激怒了日本当局，当局立即派兵逮捕徐鸿发及其手下，但这些人四散逃匿，藏身于浦东各处。

徐鸿发遂求助于顾裕声（Koo Yu Sung），顾曾任日本特务机关翻译。徐许诺，若陈丞能推荐徐担任亚洲复兴救国军第一连副连长一职，并让其部下在该连服役，则向陈丞行贿四万元。

（批：原件在 D 8945）

Subject Japanese and Chinese Troops in Nantao - transferred

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

The 1,400 Japanese and 600 Chinese troops,
who arrived in Nantao and vicinity on June 16 and
whose object, it is rumoured, is to bring pressure
to bear with a view to effecting the retrocession
of the Catholic Church area at Zikawei, were transferred
to some unknown destination during the night of June
21/22.

It has been confidentially learned that
the French Concession authorities have reached an
understanding with the Japanese authorities regarding
the Catholic Church area but particulars are unknown.
This is borne out by the fact that at 10.15 a.m.,
June 22, three armed Japanese Military Police entered
the Chiao Tung University from Loh Ka Loo, O.O.L.,
via Avenue Haig, and at 10.45 a.m., they left the
University and proceeded along Hungjao Road to the
Catholic Church area, without interference and
escort from the French Authorities.

事由 南市日军及华军 - 调离

由 督察员 潘连璧 制作 由 督察员 Crawford 转呈。

6月16日抵达南市及附近地区的1,400名日军和600名华军，据传其目的是施加压力，以求收回徐家汇天主教堂区域，这批部队已于6月21/22日夜间的转移至某未知目的地。

据密悉，法租界当局已与日本当局就天主教堂区域达成谅解，但详情不明。以下事实佐证了这一说法：6月22日上午10时15分，三名武装日本宪兵从欧战纪念碑（O.O.L.）的罗家路（Loh Ka Loo），经由海格路进入交通大学，并于上午10时45分离开大学，沿虹桥路前往天主教堂区域，全程未受法国当局干涉，亦无法国当局护送。

regarded by the Japanese as a territorial encroachment

SHANGHAI TIMES.

DEC 1 3 1939

NO KOREAN TROOPS
NEAR SHANGHAI

Japanese Deny Reports
Of Manchoukuo Troops
Being In Nantao

Japanese military authorities in
Shanghai yesterday categorically
dismissed as "ridiculous" a report
attributed to Chinese press sources
printed by an English-language
morning daily to the effect that
"9,000 Formosan and Manchoukuo
troops" were now stationed in
Nantao on the southeastern limits
of the French Concession.

Manchoukuo troops, a Japanese
military spokesman declared, are
not being used outside of the
borders of their own Empire.

"As to Formosan effectives," the
spokesman declared," there are no
such troops in the Japanese Army.
Formosan subjects are not subject
to conscription and consequently
cannot serve in the Japanese
Army."

The spokesman pointed out that
it was only recently that Japanese
subjects of Korean extraction
were being permitted to enlist in
the Japanese Army as volunteers,
as they also were not subject to
military service. Only about 2,000
such volunteers had been accepted
so far and these were still under-
going training in Chosen, the
spokesman pointed out.

D. S. Pan
(印：Q 1/2)
Shin

《字林西报》。

1939年12月13日

上海附近无朝鲜军队

日本人否认有关伪满军队
驻扎南市的报道

上海日本军方当局昨日断然驳斥了一则据称源自中文报刊并由一家英文早报刊登的报道，该报道称“9,000名台湾和伪满军队”现驻扎在法租界东南边缘的南市。

一位日本军方发言人宣称，伪满军队并未在其帝国边境之外使用。

“至于台湾兵力，”该发言人宣称，“日本军队中没有此类部队。台湾臣民不服兵役，因此不能在日军中服役。”

该发言人指出，直到最近，朝鲜裔日本臣民才被允许以志愿者身份加入日本军队，因为他们也不服兵役。发言人指出，迄今为止仅接受了约2,000名此类志愿者，且这些人仍在朝鲜接受训练。

D. S. Pan
（印：Q 1/2）
Shin

Shun Pao dated December 10 :- 11-12-29 (AM)

FORMOSAN AND MANCHUKUOAN SOLDIERS IN NANTAO AND HONGKEW

On December 7 and 8, more than 9,000
Formosan and Manchukuoan soldiers were transferred to
Nantao from Wuhu. The new arrivals were accommodated in
schools and guilds in Nantao. The soldiers wear shabby
uniforms and they seem to be in bad need of winter
necessities. During the night of December 7 and 8,
three Manchukuoan soldiers dashed into some houses in
the vicinity of a Police outpost at Great East Gate,
Nantao, and asked for blankets but when the inmates
refused to give anything to the intruders, the latter
stabbed an old housekeeper to death.
These soldiers constitute a direct menace
to peace and order in Nantao and the residents are now
devising ways and means to ensure their safety. It is
further learned that several foreign style buildings which
had escaped damage during the war have been prepared
for the accommodation of several tens of thousands of
Japanese soldiers who will be transferred to Nantao in
the course of the next few days. During the past two
days, approximately 3,000 Manchukuoan and Formosan
soldiers have arrived in Hongkew.

1939年12月10日《申报》:- 11-12-29 (上午)

南市和虹口的台湾及伪满士兵

12月7日和8日，9,000多名台湾和伪满士兵从芜湖调往南市。新抵达的人员被安置在南市的学校和会馆中。士兵们穿着破旧的制服，似乎非常缺乏冬季必需品。12月7日和8日夜间，三名伪满士兵冲进南市大东门警察岗亭附近的一些房屋，索要毯子，但当住户拒绝向闯入者提供任何物品时，后者刺死了一名老管家。
这些士兵对南市的和平与秩序构成直接威胁，居民们正在想方设法确保自身安全。另获悉，几栋在战争中幸免于难的西式建筑已准备好容纳数万名将在未来几天内调往南市的日本士兵。在过去两天里，约有3,000名伪满和台湾士兵抵达虹口。

REPORT
Date December 9, 1939.

Subject. Manchukuo troops arrived at Nantao.

Made by J.I. Pan Lien-pih, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

About 12,000 Manchukuo troops were transferred
to Shanghai from Wuhu by the Japanese Military
Authorities on December 7 and 8th, 1939. 3,000 are
stationed in Civic Centre (Niangwan), and the remaining
9,000 are stationed at the following places in Nantao:-
(1) St. Joseph's Institute for the Poor (Sing Poo Yoh
Jaung 新普育堂 ), Kuo Foo (國貨路) road.
(2) In dwelling houses at Tan Pu Jao (打浦橋), near
the south end of Rue Pere Robert.
(3) Former building of the Woosung-Shanghai Constabulary,
Ching Joh Road (警局路), near Small South Gate.
(4) Lung Men Villa (龍门邨), Boon Lai Road (Small
West Gate).
(5) Hunan Guild (湖南會館), Arsenal Road.
(6) Hwei Ning (徽甯會館) Guild, Arsenal Road.

These troops are natives of Manchuria and wear
uniforms similar to those of the Japanese Army. The
officers are Japanese and Formosans. The discipline
among the troops is very lax, and upon arrival they
searched for cotton quilts in the residences near where
they were quartered causing a panic among the Nantao
population.

According to information from a usually
reliable source, a total of some 90,000 Manchukuo
troops are to be concentrated in Nantao before December
15, 1939 the idea behind this being to intimidate the
French Authorities and so accelerate the negotiations

主题. 伪满军队抵达南市。

制作人 J.I. Pan Lien-pih，转呈人 D.I. Crawford。

1939年12月7日和8日，日本军方当局将约12,000名伪满军队从芜湖调往上海。其中3,000人驻扎在市中心（江湾），其余9,000人驻扎在南市以下地点：-
(1) 新普育堂 (Sing Poo Yoh Jaung)，国货路。
(2) 打浦桥 (Tan Pu Jao) 的住宅内，靠近罗伯神父路南端。
(3) 原吴淞上海警察局大楼，警局路，靠近小南门。
(4) 龙门邨 (Lung Men Villa)，蓬来路（小西门）。
(5) 湖南会馆，兵工厂路。
(6) 徽甯会馆，兵工厂路。

这些士兵是满洲人，穿着与日本军队相似的制服。军官是日本人和台湾人。部队纪律非常松散，抵达后他们在驻地附近的住宅中搜寻棉絮被褥，引起南市居民的恐慌。

据一个通常可靠的消息来源称，总计约90,000名伪满军队将于1939年12月15日前集中在南市，此举背后的意图是恐吓法国当局，从而加速谈判

Under the auspices of the Nantao District
Administrative Office of the "Shanghai City Government,"
a new organization to be known as the "Shanghai
Municipality Nantao Chamber of Commerce," came into
existence on November 10, 1939, with offices at 122
Ning Woo Road, City. CHANG PING DZ (張彬文),
aged 56, a native of Shanghai, and proprietor of the
Dong Shing (同鑫) Rice Shop, 116-118 Dah Ching
Road, and TSEU SHIEN NGOH (周顯岳), aged 42,
native of Kunshan, and owner of the Van Woo (萬和)

NANTAO CHAMBER OF COMMERCE FORMED

The Nantao Chamber of Commerce formed by
the Political Affairs Administration of Nantao, was
inaugurated at a meeting held on November 10 when Chang
Ping-dz (張彬如) was elected Chairman of the Chamber,
Chow Shien-ngoh (周顯岳), Vice-Chairman, and Li Fei-sung

Chairman, was formerly an usher in the defunct Sin Wu Tai

Subject. Rice Situation in Nantao and Pootung.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Nantao

The supply of rice in Nantao is monopolized by the Nantao Ming Sung Rice and Paddy Association, 377 Min Kuo Road, Nantao, which was formed in March, 1940. This Association is sponsored principally by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, which firms are the agents permitted by the Japanese authorities to purchase rice in the producing areas.

The Association at present distributes a total of some 70 bags of rice (See Mee), a total of 7 tons, to rice shops in Nantao every day. There is a stock of approximately 500 bags stored on the Association premises. The Association obtains its supplies from rice stored in Japanese godowns in Hongkew.

Rice shops purchasing supplies from the Association must first deposit with the Association a minimum sum of Yen 500, and each shop receives a quantity of rice equivalent to 90% of the value of deposits.

Although according to the regulations of the Association, purchases of rice are not permitted from sources other than the Association, the rice shops are at present permitted to buy rice from farmers bringing the grain from suburban cities. Purchases are also made from dealers in

制作人：督察员 Ian Lien Iih 转呈人：督察员 Crawford

5月5日，位于南市林国路377号的南市灵松米谷公会向南市各米店发出通函通知，内容如下：
“此后，南市有意从本公会购买大米的米店，必须首先向公会存入至少200日元作为购货保证金。米店随后可从公会购买2包大米。如需额外的大米，每包需追加100日元作为担保。如果前次交易的余额达到200日元，米店在申请进一步购买时无需再存入更多保证金。”
公会采取这一新措施引起了南市米店业主的愤慨，这些业主大多属于较贫困的小商人阶层。
5月7日上午9时，约50名南市米店代表前往位于南市蓬莱路伊索卡的南市区行政公署和驻南市日本军方联络部求助，当局承诺将与公会管理层进行谈判

DATE 18/ 4/ 40

The Nantao Ming Sung Rice and Paddy
Association (南市民生米穀公會) came into
existence on March 15, 1940, with an office on
the former premises of the Chinese Flour Exchange,
377 Min Kuo Road, Nantao. The Association was
sponsored jointly by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and
Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, with permission from
the Special Service Section of the Japanese Military.
Pan Seu Zung (潘守仁), owner of the
Kung Ping (公平) Rice Shop, 4655 Robison Road,
who is believed to have been on intimate terms with
the Japanese ever since the January 28 Incident of
1932, is also interested in the formation of this
Association. Pan Seu Zung is at present in Hongkong
but has appointed one Zau Lien Sung (趙蓮生),
ex-C.P.C. of the French Police, follower of Doo
Yueh Sung and notorious loafer in the French
Concession, to handle his affairs in Shanghai.
Zau is also connected with gambling dens in the
Western District and has amassed a large fortune
from this source.
Following its inauguration on March 15, the
promoters invited Chang Ping Sz (張彬如),
owner of Doong Shing (同鑫) Rice Shop, 116-8
Loo Shiang Yuen Road, and Chairman of the Nantao
Chamber of Commerce, and Yu Ching Wu (于經武),

南市明松米谷公会（南市民生米穀公會）于1940年3月15日成立，办公地点设在南市民国路377号原中国面粉交易所旧址。该公会由三井物产株式会社和三菱商事株式会社共同发起，并获得了日本军方特务机关的许可。
公平米店（Kung Ping Rice Shop）老板潘守仁（Pan Seu Zung），地址罗宾逊路4655号，据信自1932年一·二八事变以来一直与日本人关系密切，他也参与了该公会的组建。潘守仁目前在香港，但他任命了赵莲生（Zau Lien Sung）在上海处理其事务。赵是前法捕房华探长，杜月笙的门徒，也是法租界 notorious 的游手好闲之徒（原文用词，意指臭名昭著的混混/无赖）。赵还与西区赌窟有关联，并由此积累了大量财富。
继3月15日成立之后，发起人邀请了同鑫米店（Doong Shing Rice Shop）老板、南市商会主席张彬如（Chang Ping Sz），地址路祥园路116-8号，以及于经武（Yu Ching Wu），

The shops must also exhibit outside their premises

Association and these will be sold at $0.80 each.

The daily supply of rice by the
International Relief Committee into the Refugee
Zone, Nantao, which was prevented by the Japanese
troops stationed there on March 18th was permitted
to resume on March 23th, 1940, following lengthy
negotiations by the Refugee Zone Supervisory
Committee of the International Relief Committee.
No untoward incident occurred while the supply
of rice was discontinued.

With regard to the Nantao Ling Sung
Rice and Paddy Trade Association ( 南市民生米
穀公會 ), 377 Lin Kuo Road, Nantao, which has
for its object the monopoly of the sale of rice
in the Nantao area, no activities directed at
obtaining a monopoly have yet come into notice.

Date March 20, 1940.

Subject Nantao Situation - supply of rice.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason

On March 18, 1940, two truck loads of
rice belonging the International Relief Committee,
and being transported to the Nantao Refugee
Zone for the use of the refugees housed there,
were stopped by a Japanese sentry on duty at Rue
Chateau d'Eau. Negotiations for the entry of
the rice into the refugee zone have been
commenced by Rev. Father Jacquinot who is in
charge of the zone in question. No success
has attended his efforts so far but further
efforts are being made.

Some 100 bags of foreign rice are
transported daily to the refugee zone by the
International Relief Committee but no trouble
has ever been experienced before. This incident

Date: March 18th, 1940.

Subject. Establishment of the Nantao Popular Welfare and Rice Distribution Society.

Made by. D. S. Kamashita. Forwarded by. Supt. J. Mason.

With reference to the attached extracts from the March 14th issue of the North China Daily News and the Shanghai Times regarding the establishment of the "Nantao Popular Welfare & Rice Distribution Society" (南市民生米穀公會), enquiries show that this society was established recently on Minkuo Road, Nantao, with a capital of $2,500,000 after understanding had been reached with the Japanese Military authorities and the Social Affairs Bureau of the Shanghai City Government. The object of the society, it is stated, is to relieve the shortage of daily necessities in Nantao.

As a first step, the society is at present distributing rice and in future other food stuff will be sold. The promoters of this society are Mr. H. Yamaguchi, manager of the Daimaru Yoko on North Szechuen Road, Mr. T. Takaki, Proprietor of the Fukuki Yoko on Kiangse Road, two other Japanese, Mr. T. Ohi and Mr. H. Kurosaki, and three Chinese, Mr. Fan Yung Hwa (潘榮華), Mr. Woo Ziang Tsang (吳翔章) and Mr. Wong Kwang Sz (王匡士). It is stated that the Tung Lai Bank (東萊銀行) and Bank of East Asia (東亞銀行) will give financial support to the society.

D. S. Kamashita
D. C. (Special Branch).

Subject (in full) Nantao Refugee Zone - charity rice for residents.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Glasford O.

The issue of half price to the 19,000 poor people
living in the Nantao Refugee Zone, which was commenced
by the Committee of the International Refugee Relief
Association, on September 9, 1939, discontinued on
September 30, 1939.

About 5,000 out of the 19,000 persons were found
by the Committee to be so poor that they were unable
to support themselves. They are consequently
accommodated like refugees in a Refugee Camp on the
former premises of the Chinese Flour Exchange, 240
Boulevard des Republiques and are given 6 ounces of
free rice each every day.

The Committee of the International Refugee
Relief Association, Nantao, is contemplating
conducting an investigation into the number of
destitute persons now staying in the Refugee Zone,
City, with a view to affording them free accommodation
in a new camp to be established in the premises of

During the morning of September 9, about

residents in the Refugee Zone, Nantao, called at
the Nantao Office of the International Refugee
Relief Association, 233 Foo Pong Road, City, and
requested the Committee to rescind its decision

agreed to continue the supply of free rice in
quantities of 2½ ounces each instead of 5 ounces as
previously granted, for a period of one week,

The International Refugee Relief Association
has decided to cease the daily supply of free rice
(five ounces each) to the 19,000 residents other
than those accommodated in various camps, in the

August 3. 19xx Am.

Central China Daily News and KuoMin Daily News :-

YOUTHS' CORPS TO BE DISBANDED

Since its establishment, the Youths' Corps in
Nantao has achieved remarkable results in its work. Some time
ago owing to the fact that the place was full of lawless elements,
the Corps established a Self-Defence Section at No. 51 Kao Tung
Ka Street, Loo Hsiang Yuen Road, Nantao, with Chow Foo-dah
(周富大) as Chief. Its duty was to co-operate with the Police
and the military in the maintenance of peace and order in the
Refugee Zone. Now order has been restored and the district is
gradually moving towards prosperity. Moreover, the police
strength of the locality is sufficient to maintain peace and
order in the whole district. Consequently, it has been found
unnecessary to continue the Self-Defence Section. An order for
its disbandment was issued yesterday by the Officer-in-Charge of
the Youths' Corps. Captain Zia Ya has been detailed to take
over all the documents of the disbanding section.

19xx年8月3日 上午。

《华中日报》和《国民日报》：-

青年团将解散

自成立以来，南市青年团在工作中取得了显著成效。前段时间，由于该地区不法之徒充斥，青年团在南市鲁香园路高墩卡街51号设立了自卫队，由周富大（Chow Foo-dah）担任队长。其职责是与警察和军队合作，维护难民区的和平与秩序。如今秩序已恢复，该地区正逐步走向繁荣。此外，当地的警力足以维持整个地区的和平与秩序。因此，认为没有必要继续保留自卫队。青年团负责人昨日发布了解散命令。夏亚（Zia Ya）上尉已被指派接管被解散部门的所有文件。

On April 25, 1939, the 1st Company of
the Nantao Self-Defence Corps ( 南市自衛團 )
was formed with headquarters in the premises of
the Huh Chung Coal Briquette Company, Nan Moo Tao,
City. The corps numbering 70 are all ex-members
of a guerilla band formerly operating in the suburbs
of Shanghai and are commanded by one Tu Tien Bang
( 杜天鵬 ), Chief of the 1st Company, who has
Mr. Horikawa ( 堀川 ), Chief of the Nantao
Section of the Japanese Military Special Service
Department, as his adviser. The corps are all
in civilian attire but wear a white cloth armlet
bearing the characters: "Nantao Self-Defence Corps
of the Japanese Military Special Service Department".
They are stated to be equipped with some 10 rifles,
20 Mauser pistols and some 20 automatics.

Date July 4, 1940

Subject Refugee Zone in Nantao - Situation.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

At 7 p.m., June 30, 1940, the Supervisory
Committee of the Nantao Refugee Zone, 235 Fong Fang Road
(方浜路), Nantao, wound up their affairs. The Super-
visory Committee distributed one-month's free rice from
the stocks left to the refugees accommodated in the Zone
on June 30th, but the refugees when collecting the rice
for their meals on that date saw 150 bags of rice stored
on the committee premises. The staff at this time were
attempting to shift this rice to the Sing Po Yo Tang
(新普育堂 ) Benevolent Institution on Kuo Hoo (國貨 )
Road, Nantao, when they were prevented by a horde of
refugees who stole the rice before it could be transported.
The Police in the vicinity took no action.

A number of refugees are still living in the
Refugee Zone Area in spite of the dissolution of the
above Committee.

The Japanese Military Special Service Section,
Nantao Branch and the Shanghai City Government, it is
reported, are to take care of those refugees who are
definitely infirm, disabled or homeless, when the general
liquidation of the other refugees has taken place.

Regarding the "French Refugee Lottery", there will
be two or three more drawings the proceeds of which will
be allotted to the Nantao Refugee Hospital for its upkeep.
This Hospital is sponsored by Father Jacquinot.

制作人 巡官 潘连璧 转呈人 巡官 Crawford

1940年6月30日晚7时，位于南市方浜路（Fong Fang Road）235号的南市难民区监察委员会结束了其事务。监察委员会将库存剩余的一个月免费大米分发给6月30日居住在区内的难民，但在当天领取口粮时，难民们看到委员会驻地储存了150袋大米。此时工作人员正试图将这些大米运往南市国货路（Kuo Hoo Road）的新普育堂（Sing Po Yo Tang）慈善机构，但被一群难民阻止，大米在运输前被抢走。附近的警察未采取行动。

尽管上述委员会已解散，仍有不少难民居住在难民区区域内。

据报道，在日本军方特务机关南市分部和上海市政府对其他难民进行普遍清理安置后，将由他们照顾那些确属老弱病残或无家可归的难民。

关于“法商难民彩票”，还将进行两到三次抽奖，所得款项将拨给南市难民医院用于其维持运营。该医院由饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）赞助。

Date June 21 19 40

Subject: Refugee Zone in Nantao to wind up affairs.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

On June 16, 1940, the Supervisory Committee
of the Refugee Zone in Nantao was renamed "The
Rehabilitation Committee of the Refugee Zone in Nantao"
(南市難民區善後委員會) and Mr. A. Jaspar, Directeur,
Ecole Primaire de Lagrene, who was one of the members
of the Supervisory Committee, was nominated Chairman
of the Rehabilitation Committee.

It is learned that the Rehabilitation
Committee has decided to wind up the affairs of the
Nantao Refugee Zone, which was established at the end
of 1937 by Father Jacquinot, and to liquidate the
refugees at present under its care. .

It is estimated that there are at present
some 19,000 male and female refugees accommodated in
the various camps in the Zone and the Rehabilitation
Committee expects that they will be disposed off
before July 15, 1940, with the exception of some 300
who are infirm and disabled and who will be transferred
to the Poo Yo Tang Benevolent Institution in Nantao.

Detailed measures regarding the proposed
repatriation are now under discussion.

制作人 巡官 潘连璧 转呈人 巡官 Crawford。

1940年6月16日，南市难民区监察委员会更名为“南市难民区善后委员会”（南市難民區善後委員會），原监察委员会委员之一、拉格内小学（Ecole Primaire de Lagrene）校长 A. Jaspar 先生被提名为善后委员会主席。

据悉，善后委员会已决定结束由饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）于1937年底建立的南市难民区的事务，并遣散目前由其照管的难民。

据估计，目前区内各营地收容的男女难民约有19,000人，善后委员会预计除约300名老弱病残者将转移至南市普育堂慈善机构外，其余难民将在1940年7月15日前得到安置。

关于拟议的遣返措施的详细方案目前正在讨论中。

June 19, 1940. Afternoon Translation

Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao :-

REFUGEE ZONE IN NANTAO TO BE WOUND UP AT THE END OF JUNE

As the result of a discussion by the
Rehabilitation Committee, after the departure of Father
Jacquinot from Shanghai, it was decided that the Refugee
Zone in Nantao be wound up at the end of this month.
Young and able-bodied refugees will be issued with
provisions for half a month and will then be repatriated,
whilst the old, weak and disabled refugees will be removed
to Poo Yoh Tong Benevolent Institution (普育堂).
The French Vice-Consul in Shanghai was
entrusted with this work by Father Jacquinot before his
departure as the former is a member of the Supervisory
Committee of the Refugee Zone in Nantao.
It is not known whether the Relief Lottery will
be suspended. There have been in all 20 drawings of the
Lottery; the 21st will be drawn on June 21.

《新闻报》和《申报》：-

南市难民区将于六月底结束

在饶家驹神父离开上海后，经善后委员会讨论，决定于本月底结束南市难民区。年轻力壮的难民将获发半个月的生活物资，随后被遣返，而老弱病残难民将被移送至普育堂慈善机构（Poo Yoh Tong Benevolent Institution）。
饶家驹神父在离沪前将此工作委托给上海法国副领事，因为后者是南市难民区监察委员会的成员。
尚不清楚救济彩票是否会暂停。彩票总共已开奖20次；第21次将于6月21日开奖。

antagonistic attitude adopted toward him by several of
the managers of refugee camps under the control of the
International Relief Committee. He has now been replaced
by Mr. Koo Lung (顧  ), a returned law student from
France.

reinstatement by Father Jacquinot on his return from abroad,

With reference to the attached xxxxxx from the Life
Daily News and other local newspapers dated February 26, 1938,
quoting a "Domei News Agency" report, enquiries have been made
and the following information obtained.

Mr. Pan Tse Chieh (潘志傑) was the director and Mr.
Tai Chong Ling (戴昌林), associate director of the Nantao
Head Office of the International Relief Committee, 235 Fang
Bang Road, Nantao, which was formerly occupied by the Nantao
Fire Brigade.

Mr. Pan Tse Chieh is a very obstinate and proud man, and
there are many instances in which he has had differences with the
other members of the International Relief Committee on questions
pertaining to the relief of refugees. Recently Mr. Pan Tse
Chieh clashed with the Japanese Military Police in Nantao, over
an order issued by them that ten rickshas belonging to the Head
Office of the International Relief Committee should have passes
issued by the Nantao Police Bureau before being used in the zone.
Mr. Pan objected to this new procedure, which was of no avail,
and dissatisfied with the state of affairs, Mr. Pan tendered
his resignation on February 24. Being a close associate of
Mr. Pan and in sympathy with him, Mr. Tai Chong Ling, assistant
director of the Nantao Head Office of the International Relief
Committee, tendered his resignation also on the same day.

It is reported that up to the present, no officials have
been appointed to succeed Mr. Pan Tse Chieh and Mr. Tai Chong Ling.

RESIGNATIONS FROM NANTAO REFUGEE RELIEF COMMITTEE

The Domei News Agency supplies the following
report:-
On February 24 Messrs. Pan (潘) and Tai (戴)
and the Chiefs of the various districts sent in their
joint resignation to the Nantao Refugee Relief Committee,
which is under charge of Father Jacquinot. They stated
that the relief work that is being undertaken by foreigners
is of no practical benefit to the Chinese people.
It is possible that the resignation of these
people is due to their fear of being implicated in the
cases of malfeasance of office committed by certain other
members of the Committee who have absconded.
The whereabouts of the resigned Chinese committee-
men are unknown. The relief work in the Refugee Zone
sponsored by Father Jacquinot has come to a standstill.
Efforts are being made by the Committee to secure new
committeemen, but the reports circulated regarding the
above affairs are deterring people from joining.

HELPING NANTAO
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—Will you kindly give space
to this letter regarding "Good-Will
Industries" in Nantao. We have
tried out this self-help or employ-
ment method of reconstruction in
Nantao for three months and find
that it fills a very real need. Many
Shanghai friends have "Good-Will
Bags" in their homes and many
have sent gift of money. We hope
that these gifts may continue that
the work may be developed. At
present we are helping about 200
unemployed men and women in the
work rooms daily and about 90
more with free distribution of
clothing or with small household
utensils.
Clothing and household articles
are also sold at the "Good-Will"
stores at low prices to the very
poor who are not working at the
"Good-Will" centre. Workers and
neighbours alike receive free
medical aid at the clinic daily.
About $1,000 per month is required
to help the work going at the pre-
sent scale. Routine collection of
old clothing and household goods is
also necessary to provide work for
the workers.
We are now withdrawing from
"Good-Will" for furlough but the
relief project for the poor beyond
the safety zone in Nantao is being
carried on by others. Misses
Ricketts and Russell, of Hangchow,
are working in connection with the
work room in the Nantao Christian
Institute. Mr. Ralph White, of Soo-
chow, is serving as treasurer.
Will those who wish to help
finance this programme of self-help
by gifts, memorial cheques, etc.,
please send them payable to Mr.
Ralph White, at 169 Yuen Ming
Yuen Road.
We wish to express our apprecia-
tion of the interest in and support
given by the many who have help-
ed to establish "Good-Will In-
dustries" in Shanghai as this has
made possible far more help toward
regarding a livelihood than one can
realize for these hundreds in great
need.
MR. AND MRS. WILMOT D. BOONE
Shanghai, June 24, 1938.
page_data.zh:
援助南市
编辑，
《字林西报》
先生，—恳请贵报刊登这封关于南市“Good-Will Industries”（善举工业社）的信函。我们在南市试行这种自助或就业重建方法已有三个月，发现它确实满足了非常切实的需求。许多上海朋友家中都有“Good-Will Bags”（善举袋），许多人还捐赠了款项。我们希望这些捐赠能持续下去，以便这项工作得以发展。目前，我们每天在工作室帮助约200名失业男女，并通过免费分发衣物或小型家用器具帮助另外约90人。
衣物和家居用品也以低价出售给那些不在“Good-Will”中心工作的极度贫困者。工人和邻居每天都能在诊所获得免费医疗援助。
要维持目前规模的工作，每月需要约1,000美元。常规收集旧衣物和家居用品也是必要的，以便为工人提供工作。
我们现在因休假而退出“Good-Will”项目，但南市安全区以外针对穷人的救济项目正由其他人继续开展。杭州的 Ricketts 小姐和 Russell 小姐正在南市基督教研究所的工作室相关工作。苏州的 Ralph White 先生担任司库。
愿通过捐款、纪念支票等方式资助这一自助计划的人士，请将款项寄至圆明园路169号，收款人为 Ralph White 先生。
我们要表达对众多帮助在上海建立“Good-Will Industries”的人士的兴趣和支持的感激之情，因为这为数百名急需帮助的人提供了远超人们想象的谋生帮助。
WILMOT D. BOONE 先生及夫人
上海，1938年6月24日。

Subject. NANTAO SITUATION - Increase in public ricsha licence
fees - collection of copper coins.

Made by. J.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by.

（印：SHAH POLICE 14 JUNE 1939 COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

Towards the end of April, 1939, the Nantao
Traffic Office of the Bureau of Public Utilities of
the "Shanghai City Government", Wen Kao Road, Nantao,
announced that with effect from May 1, 1939, the
licence fees for public ricshas would be increased from
50 cents to 80 cents per month. At first, the ricsha
owners and their pullers refused to comply with the
order, and petitions were addressed to the Bureau of
Public Utilities requesting the cancellation of the
increase. On their request being rejected, the ricsha
owners complied with the order with effect from June 1
but reduced the number of ricshas in operation.

Originally there were altogether some 1,000
ricshas in operation, but now there are approximately
750, the others having been put aside because of the
increase in licence fees and lack of business.

-----

During the past few days, certain Chinese
have been engaged in collecting copper coins from the
Chinese people living in various parts in Nantao, at
200 coppers for $1 (the proper rate should be 300
coppers for $1). It is reported that these persons
exchanged the coppers at 160 pieces for $1 from the
Japanese.

Commr of Police
Sir

Made by. D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by. C. Crawford

With a view to offsetting the financial difficul-
ties experienced by his office, Mr. Sung sze-ching
(沈書經), Chief of the Nantao Administrative
Office of the Shanghai City Government, has
instructed Yue Ching-woo (于經武), Chief of the
Third Department of the Nantao Administrative Office,
to establish a "Collecting Office for the Road
Maintenance Levy" (養路費徵收所) on the
ground floor of No. 232 Boulevard Des deux Republiques.
With the consent of the Nantao Section of the Japanese
Military Special Service Department obtained, a
collecting office was established on March 12, 1939
and has been functioning ever since under the pretext
that the roadways will be kept in good repair for
the rehabilitation of the Nantao Area. All commodities
on vehicles entering Nantao from the French Concession
are required to pay a rate equivalent to five per cent
of their declared value.
On March 16, 1939, Mayor Fu Siao-an, upon learning
of this new measure by the Nantao Administrative Office,
ordered the collection to cease forthwith on the
grounds as no sanction had been given by his office
for the collection. It is unlikely, however, that
this instruction will be complied with since the
Nantao Administrative Office has the support of the
Japanese Special Service Section.

Pan Lien-pih

Made by D.I. Fan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Gxxxxx

Further to Special Branch report dated March 31, 1938
on the above subject, Mr. Sung Sing Fu ( 沈心樵 ), chairman
of the Shanghai Nantao Traders' Association, was detained
on March 30 by Japanese gendarmes for having brought into
the Zone copies of the Ta Mei Wan Pao, Chinese edition of
the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, and was released at
11 a.m. April 9 on the recommendation of the "Nantao Autonomous
Commission".

Mr. Sung Sing Fu is known to have been hostile towards
the "Nantao Autonomous Commission," because the latter
organization intended taking over control of the Shanghai
Nantao Traders' Association. His resentment against the
"Nantao Autonomous Commission" was increased when Mr. Chow
Zung Fu ( 周潤甫 ), a shop proprietor in the Nantao Safety
Zone, who acted as vice chairman of the Traders' Association
and who is well versed in things Japanese, was appointed chief
of the Industrial and Commercial Section of the Autonomous
Commission.

Anxious to get rid of him, the Autonomous Commission
made the two refugees, who were arrested on March 29 for selling
copies of the Ta Mei Wan Pao in the Nantao Safety Zone, sign
a false statement implicating Mr. Sung. Before he was allowed
his freedom, he gave an undertaking that he would resign from
the Traders' Association.

The Shanghai Nantao Traders' Association suspended its
operations on April 9, and the "Nantao Autonomous Commission"
has not yet decided whether to allow the continuance of the
Traders' Association or to incorporate in the Commission.

继1938年3月31日关于上述主题的特务科报告之后，上海南市商界联合会主席沈心樵（Sung Sing Fu）先生于3月30日被日本宪兵拘留，原因是他将《大美晚报》（即《上海晚邮报与水星报》中文版）带入该区，并于4月9日上午11时经“南市自治委员会”推荐获释。

据悉，沈心樵先生对“南市自治委员会”持敌对态度，因为该组织意图接管上海南市商界联合会的控制权。当在南市安全区经营店铺的周润甫（Chow Zung Fu）先生——他担任商界联合会副主席且精通日本事务——被任命为自治委员会工商科科长时，他对“南市自治委员会”的怨恨进一步加深。

自治委员会急于除掉他，便让两名因在南市安全区贩卖《大美晚报》而于3月29日被捕的难民签署了一份诬陷沈先生的虚假供词。在获准恢复自由之前，他承诺辞去商界联合会的职务。

上海南市商界联合会已于4月9日停止运作，“南市自治委员会”尚未决定是允许商界联合会继续存在还是将其并入委员会。

Subject "Shanghai Nantao Traders' Association" - new body.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien-pih Forwarded by A. H. Logan

(批：Feb For record)
(印：21 MAR 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH)

The Shanghai Nantao Traders' Association (上海南市商界联合会), formerly known as the Nantao Safety Zone Traders' Association (南市難民區商聯會 ), was established on January 20, 1938, with an office at 775 Loo Hsiang Yuan Road, Nantao. After the Japanese military authorities took over control of the Nantao Safety Zone, the Traders' Association was ordered to cease functioning. Petitions were later submitted to the Japanese military and French Concession authorities to permit the Association to resume operations. The request was granted by both these authorities and the Association resumed operations at the beginning of February.

The duty of the Traders' Association is to transport merchandise by hand trolley from rue de la Porte du Nord and to distribute it among various traders located in the Nantao Safety Zone. With a view to preventing the traders from demanding a prohibitive price for their products, the Traders' Association checks the prices of commodities stocked by the traders with those prevailing in the Settlement and the French Concession, and post them in the office of the Association daily for the information of the residents of the Safety Zone.

The Association collects no subscription or initiation fees from members, but charge a transportation fee of .005 of the value of the commodities transported. The Association employs a staff of about thirty persons and its expenses amount to about $600 a month. The income derived in the form of transportation fees ranges between $400 and $500 a month, leaving a deficit of $100 to $200, to the liquidation of which the members equally subscribe.

主题：“上海南市商界联合会”——新机构。

由督察员范连璧（Fan Lien-pih）制作，由 A. H. Logan 转呈

（批：二月 存档）
（印：1938年3月21日 特务科）

上海南市商界联合会（前称南市难民区商联会）于1938年1月20日成立，办公地点位于南市老西门路775号。在日本军方接管南市安全区控制权后，该商界联合会被勒令停止活动。随后，向日本军方和法租界当局提交请愿书，请求允许该会恢复运作。这两方当局均批准了请求，该会于二月初恢复运作。

商界联合会的职责是通过手推车从北门路（rue de la Porte du Nord）运输货物，并将其分配给位于南市安全区的各个商贩。为了防止商贩对其产品索要高价，商界联合会将商贩库存商品的价格与公共租界和法租界的现行价格进行核对，并每日张贴在协会办公室，供安全区居民知晓。

该会不向会员收取会费或入会费，但对所运输商品的价值收取0.5%的运输费。该会雇佣约三十名员工，每月开支约为600美元。以运输费形式获得的收入每月在400至500美元之间，留下100至200美元的赤字，由会员均摊弥补。

Subject "Traders' Association for the Nantao Safety Zone" - formed
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-nih Forwarded by C. Crawford

A new organization to be known as the "Traders'
Association for the Nantao Safety Zone" was recently formed
by one Sung Sing Fu (沈心撫) with an office at 52 and 54
Loo Hsiang Yuan Road, Kyeu Low Dee, Nantao.
The object of the association is to help traders in
the Nantao Safety Zone in getting their supplies through
the boundary between the French Concession and Nantao. This
association was formed to succeed the proposed Nantao Branch
of the "Shanghai Citizens' Civic Association" promoted by
Mr. Loh Fah-nong (陸伯鴻), who was assassinated, and the
proposed Nantao Branch was then abolished.
The new organization was promoted by Sung Sing Fu,
Sien Kwan Sung (冼冠生), Chang Ling Ju (張楞如) and
others, but the prime mover was Sung Sing Fu, who was formerly
chairman of the Nantao District Citizens' Federation. The
remaining persons including Sien Kwan Sung, who is the
manager of the Kwang Sung Yuen Confectionery on Nanking Road,
only lent their names to the project and have no interest
therein.

August 27, 1941.

Situation in Nantao

According to information from Nantao Police
authorities, on the morning of August 25, a party of
Japanese sentries and Chinese policemen whilst on duty
in the vicinity of Chung Shan Road near Hungjao, were
suddenly attacked by a number of Chinese plain-clothes
men with pistols. After the shooting, it was discovered
that two Japanese sentries were missing while three of
four policemen of the Nantao police were wounded.

As from 5 p.m. even date, the Nantao Police
authorities commenced precautionary measures. A sergeant
armed with a mauser pistol and 2 or 3 constables armed
with rifles were posted at each of the iron gates on
the borders of the French Concession, and five constables
armed with rifles were guarding the entrances of police
sub-stations in Nantao.

February 7, 1941. Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News and National Herald :-

A "FRIENDLY" ACT

Of late, residents leaving or entering Nantao
and Tousewei with their goods have often been molested by
Japanese soldiers and sometimes the goods are confiscated.
At about 9.25 a.m. yesterday, a similar case
took place at the iron gate on Sin Chiao Ka (新橋街) in
Nantao. A coolie was carrying one hundred catties of coal
briquettes into the Foreign Settlements. This was observed
by the Japanese soldiers, who, without saying a word, kicked
at the coal briquette baskets and overturned them. The coolie
was not allowed to pick up the briquettes. The soldiers,
moreover, ground the briquettes to powder under their heels
and some even threw the briquettes at the face of the coolie.
Eventually the coolie left with baskets empty.
This is another example of the so-called
"rapprochement" and "friendliness."

《中美日报》和《国民新闻》：

一种“友好”行为

近来，携带货物进出南市和土山湾的居民经常受到日本士兵的骚扰，有时货物会被没收。
昨天上午9时25分左右，南市新桥街（Sin Chiao Ka）的铁门处发生了类似案件。一名苦力正挑着一百斤煤球进入外国租界。日本士兵看到了这一幕，二话不说，踢翻了装煤球的篮子。苦力不被允许捡起煤球。此外，士兵们还用脚后跟将煤球踩成粉末，有些人甚至将煤球扔向苦力的脸。最终，苦力空着篮子离开。
这是所谓“亲善”和“友好”的又一个例子。

Sept. 26, 40.

Political Police Bureau bans sale of pro-Chungking newspapers
in Nantao - Registration of armed guards in the employ of gambling dens.

With reference to the attached translation of
an article entitled "Political Police Bureau Bans
Sale of Newspapers Harmful to the Republic : Shops
And Amusement Resorts Instructed Not To Advertise
In These Newspapers," which appeared in the September
23 issue of the Central China Daily News, enquiries
show that the term "newspapers harmful to the Republic"
contained in the original text of the article refers
to all vernacular newspapers which are anti-Wang Ching
Wei in nature.

According to information obtained from a
source closely connected with the Political Police
Bureau, the latest notification instructing shops and
amusement resorts not to advertise in pro-Chungking
papers was issued for the purpose of making known
the intention of the Bureau to eventually interfere
with the operation of the gambling dens in Nantao,
while the banning of the sale of pro-Chungking
newspapers in Nantao can only be interpreted as a
subterfuge on the part of the Bureau, when it is
remembered that ever since the occupation of Nantao
by the Japanese Army at the end of 1937, such papers
have not been allowed to be brought into the area
and that the financial position of the shops in
Nantao does not warrant the insertion of commercial
advertisements in newspapers.

1940年9月26日。

政治警察部禁止在南市出售亲重庆报纸 - 登记赌场雇佣的武装警卫。

关于附上的《华中日报》9月23日刊登的一篇题为“政治警察部禁止出售有害民国之报纸：商店及娱乐场所奉令不得在此类报纸刊登广告”的文章译文，经查询，该文原文中所称“有害民国之报纸”系指所有具有反汪精卫性质的白话文报纸。

据与政治警察部关系密切的消息来源获悉，最新发布的禁止商店和娱乐场所在亲重庆报纸上刊登广告的通知，旨在表明该部最终将干预南市赌场经营的意图；而禁止在南市出售亲重庆报纸，只能被视为该部的一种借口，因为众所周知，自1937年底日军占领南市以来，此类报纸一直不被允许带入该地区，且南市商店的财务状况也不支持在报纸上刊登商业广告。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

In order to attract patrons to visit their
establishments, the gambling dens in Nantao, such as
the Si Yuen Gambling Den and the Loh Yuen Gambling
Den, have been daily advertising in the columns of
pro-Wang newspapers while on occasion they have also
advertised in the columns of pro-Chungking newspapers.
Since all these gambling dens are operating under the
supervision or protection of the Shanghai City
Government Police Bureau, the Political Police Bureau
has never had any share of revenue from those
establishments, hence the notification instructing them
not to insert advertisements in pro-Chungking vernacular
newspapers, which has been duly complied with.

Apart from issuing the above notification,
the Political Police Bureau on September 22nd, also
issued instructions to the gambling dens in Nantao,
calling for the registration of armed guards in their
employ and also of their firearms. It is learned,
however, that the dens have thus far ignored these
instructions.

为了吸引顾客光顾其场所，南市的赌场，如四元赌场和乐园赌场，每日均在亲汪报纸的专栏中刊登广告，偶尔也在亲重庆报纸的专栏中刊登广告。由于所有这些赌场均在上海市政府警察局监管或保护下运营，政治警察部从未从这些场所获得任何收入分成，因此，指示它们不得在亲重庆白话文报纸上刊登广告的通知已得到适当遵守。

除发布上述通知外，政治警察部还于9月22日向南市赌场发出指令，要求登记其雇佣的武装警卫及其枪支。然而据悉，各赌场迄今无视这些指令。

The Nantao Administrative Office on May 3,
1940, issued a notice urging the residents of Nantao
to pay rent at a rate equivalent to half of that
paid before the hostilities. This payment is to be
made from May 1940 for a period of three months
when new scales will be considered.

In response to the above notification, the
Nantao Tenants Association, No. 1 Tse Cen Li, Loo
Shiang Yuen Road. Kiu Hou Dien, Nantao, held a
meeting at 2 p.m. May 5. 1940 on the association
premises and passed the following resolutions.

That the instructions in the notice be opposed.
That 10% to 20% of the original rent be paid
until such time as the local situation returns
to normal.

The meeting was attended by some 80 tenants
and presided over by the chairman Tsang Ping Zu
(張彬水).

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

DEC 12 1939

Nantao Area Opened
By Authorities
Concession Officials Grant
Five Days Test

One of the iron gates separating
the French Concession from Nantao
which has been closed since the out-
break of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
was re-opened yesterday to traffic
thus making it much more convenient
for former Nantao residents to return
to their homes and also to rehabilitate
the Native City which was partially
destroyed by the war. Many Chinese
re-entered Nantao yesterday through
this gate and many others were seen
entering into the Concession.

The gate is know as the Hsing
Kai Ho near the Small East Gate in
Nantao and Rue des deux Repub-
liques in the Concession. Before
the gate was re-opened people had
to travel to Nantao via Pootung or
the Western District. Whether or not
the gate will permanently remain
open remains to be seen, but it was
reported last night that authorities
in the Concession had decided to re-
open it for five days only as an
experiment.

With both French and Chinese
police on hand in their respective
areas those entering Nantao were
required to show their good citizen
certificates issued by the Japanese.
Formerly, it required also a French
Concession pass but commencing
yesterday the latter passes might be
discarded. While many people, now
refugees in foreign areas, want to
return to Nantao to visit their houses
it is reported that many are looking
for chances for establishing gambling
houses there.

It will be recalled that Mayor Fu
Siao-en of the new Chinese régime
in Kiangwan has requested the
authorities in the Concession to re-
open the iron gates in order to
develop Nantao but if could not be
ascertained yesterday whether or not
the action taken by the French
authorities was in accordance with
that request.

当局开放南市地区
租界官员给予五天试验期

自中日敌对行动爆发以来一直关闭的、分隔法租界与南市的铁门之一，于昨日重新对交通开放，这使得前南市居民返回家园以及重建部分被战争摧毁的华界城区变得更为便利。许多中国人昨天通过这扇大门重新进入南市，也有许多人被看到进入租界。

这扇大门被称为兴凯河（Hsing Kai Ho，音译），靠近南市的小东门和租界内的两共和国路（Rue des deux Republiques）。在大门重新开放之前，人们必须经由浦东或西区前往南市。这扇大门是否会永久保持开放尚待观察，但昨晚有报道称，租界当局决定仅将其重新开放五天作为试验。

由于法国和中国警察分别在各自区域值守，进入南市的人被要求出示由日本人签发的良民证。以前还需要法租界通行证，但从昨天开始，后者通行证可能不再需要。虽然许多现在流亡在外籍区域的难民希望返回南市查看他们的房屋，但有报道称，许多人正在寻找在那里开设赌馆的机会。

回想起来，江湾的新中国政权市长傅筱庵曾请求租界当局重新开放铁门以发展南市，但昨天无法查明法国当局采取的行动是否符合该请求。
