CHINA PRESS.
Dec. 1 1938
73 12 39

Nantao Gates Are Opened To New
Japanese Controlled · Heroin Hells

Drug-Den Keeper Declares
Dope Supplied By Japanese

A Chinese, clothed in tatters and lying dead in a deserted, ruined alleyway, with a heap of ashv loss-paper at his head, was pointed to as testimony to the ease with which heroin could be obtained in Nantao today, when a CHINA PRESS representative followed a stream of Chinese snaking into the native city following the opening of French Concession gates yesterday for the first time in two years.

“Too much heroin, too little rice,” explained an elderly Chinese, who claimed he had lived in Nantao ever since the hostilities in that area had ended. “About five beggars are found dead in the streets for this reason every day,” he added calmly.

The elderly Chinese was, in fact, himself the owner of a heroin den. It was in a small room approached by way of a tortuous dead-end and a swaying stair-case in the half-ruined hovel the man called his home, that The CHINA Press representative saw Chinese smoking white heroin powder dealt out at 10 cents a portion.

Supplied By Japanese

“The Japanese only can import this heroin from Tinghsing near Peiping. They make about $2,000 to $3,000 a month. The police (“Ta Tao”) keep a list of heroin-houses, and take money from them.”

“About 200 of these houses have existed for almost two years,” he continued. “Most of them are owned by wealthy Chinese.”

Although the population of Nantao was said to have increased by 400 per cent yesterday, the general impression received was that it was still largely deserted.

Desolate Scene

A few main roads are lined by shops and filled with the throngs and clamor of a Chinese city, a few steps away, roads lead to a land of war’s aftermath.

Whole areas that used to be crowded houses with thousands of families, lie in ruins, and the silence is broken only by a lone woman or the grating of a dog burrowing among mounds of tiles.

On the French Concession side of the main Nantao gate there is seething activity from morning to sundown.

In the narrow road leading to the gate industrious Chinese have hastily erected food stalls and primitive tea-houses, and here an old man being carried along in the heavy stream of humanity, with his few belongings on his back, or a wrinkled little woman hugging her frightened daughter behind her, stop to discourse over cups or haggle over the price of a Chinese pancake.

At the end of the road he hesitating, shouting, a slowly-moving mass of humanity squeezes itself to pass between barbed-wire barriers, it is let through without question by French Concession police and asked for their passes by “Ta Tao” policemen and Japanese sentries.

Nantao In Ruins

Along the long, wide road that leads into the cobbled streets of Nantao proper, it continues in a long never-ending stream. On the right are the closed, slightly-ruined three-storey houses that are Nantao’s skyline. On the left side of the road is French Concession territory, from which they are kept away by French police.

Most of those returning to a war-stricken city carried their property in straw mats or blankets. Almost none made use of waiting rickshas. All—even the oldest—pushed forward eagerly.

Nantao itself fitted into that strange picture that could be seen in all districts of Shanghai taking on new life after the blow of 1937.

Houses that consisted mainly of broken roofs and cracked walls leaned dangerously over forlorn lanes. Doors were barred of bricked in. Here and there a bearded Chinese sat behind a stall of cigarettes and sweetmeats, and here and there a door slightly ajar revealed people and roosters moving around in an inner courtyard.

Forlorn Remains

To the side of these roads were ruins. A massive, ornate gate was all that was left of a house. Pocked-marked with shell-holes, a skeleton building displayed advertising in flamboyant letters that once were gold. A lone column carried a blue metal disc reading “Public Telephone.” In the midst of bricks and tiles where once there must have been a temple, stood an unharmed receptacle for joss. Beside it, his long hair matted and his body dustygrey, a scavenger washed a carrot in a dirty puddle.

Further on, the roads began to take on life. More shops were seen, more people, more open doors. A large shop or two offered meat, food products and even clothing. But both the rickshas and the increasing traffic of pedestrians were moving in one direction—into the heart of Nantao.

Here the streets had the appearance of a boom town, for it was here, inquiries revealed, that 90 per cent of the thousands who had been flowing in through the Nantao gate were settling. Only people with little or hardly any money at all made their homes among the cutlying ruins.

Claimants Clash

Men, women and children milled backwards and forwards, and it was difficult to even pass through some blocks. The impression was that a large colony had descended on a desert city and was hovering anxiously in preparation to settle down.

Here an argument was in furious progress between two families who had apparently claimed an empty shop at the same time. Here a small looming mill twisted cotton into multicolored fiber, and the buzz of the carpenter’s saw putting the finishing touches on repair jobs was heard on all sides.

The great majority of the shops, which sold pretty nearly all Chinese commodities from raw meat to torchlights, however, were in operation long before the city gates were thrown open, shop-owners stated. One-fifth of the present swelled population of Nantao had lived there through the two years following the hostilities, they added. Now that prosperity seemed to be back, the shops had stocked themselves with more articles.

《大美晚报》。
1938年12月1日
73 12 39

南市大门向新的日本控制的“海洛因地狱”开放

毒窟经营者声称毒品由日本人供应

当《大美晚报》记者跟随一股蜿蜒进入华界城区的中国人流——这是两年来法租界大门首次开放——时，一名衣衫褴褛的中国人死在一条荒废的废墟小巷中，头边堆着一堆纸灰，这被指为如今在南市获取海洛因轻而易举的证据。

“海洛因太多，大米太少，”一位自称自该地区敌对行动结束以来一直居住在南市的老中国人解释道。“每天大约有五个乞丐因此死在街头，”他平静地补充道。

这位老中国人实际上本身就是一家海洛因烟馆的老板。《大美晚报》记者在那男子称为家的半毁陋室中，经过一条曲折的死胡同和摇晃的楼梯进入一个小房间，看到中国人正在吸食白色海洛因粉末，每份售价一角。

由日本人供应

“只有日本人能从北平附近的定兴进口这种海洛因。他们每月赚取约2000至3000美元。警察（‘大陶’，音译）保留海洛因房屋的名单，并向他们收钱。”

“大约200家这样的房屋已经存在了将近两年，”他继续说道。“其中大多数由富有的中国人拥有。”

尽管据说昨天南市的人口增加了400%，但给人的总体印象是那里仍然 largely 荒无人烟。

凄凉景象

几条主要道路两旁排列着商店，挤满了中国式城市的喧嚣人群，几步之外，道路通向一片战后的土地。

曾经拥挤着成千上万家庭的整个区域如今已成废墟，寂静只被一个孤独的女人或在瓦砾堆中挖掘的狗的抓挠声打破。

在南市大门的法租界一侧，从早到晚都活动频繁。

在通往大门的狭窄道路上，勤劳的中国人匆忙搭建了食品摊和简陋的茶馆，在这里，一位背着少量家当的老人随着沉重的人流被推着前行，或者一位满脸皱纹的小妇人抱着受惊的女儿停在身后，停下来边喝茶边交谈，或为一张中国饼的价格讨价还价。

在道路的尽头，犹豫着，呼喊着，缓慢移动的人群挤压着穿过带刺铁丝网屏障，法租界警察毫无疑问地放行，而“大陶”（音译）警察和日本哨兵则查验他们的通行证。

南市成为废墟

沿着通往南市铺石街道的漫长宽阔道路，人流持续不断，永无止境。右侧是封闭的、略微破损的三层楼房，构成了南市的天际线。道路左侧是法租界领土，法国警察将他们阻挡在外。

大多数返回这座饱受战争蹂躏的城市的人用草席或毯子携带财产。几乎没有人使用等候的黄包车。所有人——即使是最年长者——都急切地向前推进。

南市本身融入了上海所有地区在遭受1937年打击后重获新生的奇特景象中。

主要由破碎屋顶和开裂墙壁组成的房屋危险地倾斜在凄凉的巷道上。门被封住或用砖砌死。偶尔可以看到留着胡子的中国人坐在香烟和糖果摊后面，偶尔半开的门 reveals 人们在内部庭院中走动，还有公鸡。

凄凉的残骸

这些道路旁边是废墟。一座巨大、装饰华丽的大门是一所房子仅存的部分。一栋骨架般的建筑布满弹孔，展示着曾经金光闪闪的醒目字母广告。一根孤零零的柱子上挂着一个蓝色金属圆盘，上面写着“公用电话”。在曾经是寺庙的砖瓦堆中，立着一个完好无损的香炉。在它旁边，一个头发蓬乱、身体沾满灰尘的拾荒者正在脏水坑里洗胡萝卜。

再往前走，道路开始恢复生机。看到了更多的商店，更多的人，更多敞开的大门。一两家大商店出售肉类、食品甚至衣物。但是，无论是黄包车还是日益增加的行人交通，都朝着同一个方向移动——进入南市的中心。

这里的街道呈现出繁荣城镇的景象，因为调查显示，成千上万通过南市大门涌入的人中有90%在此定居。只有几乎没有钱的人在边缘的废墟中安家。

索赔者冲突

男人、女人和孩子来回穿梭，甚至很难穿过某些街区。给人的印象是一个大型殖民群体降临到一座荒漠城市，并焦虑地徘徊，准备定居下来。

这里，两个家庭显然同时声称拥有一家空店铺，正在进行激烈的争吵。这里，一台小型 looming mill（原文不清，可能是织布机或纺纱机）将棉花扭成彩色纤维，到处都能听到木匠锯子完成修缮工作的嗡嗡声。

然而，店主们表示，绝大多数出售从生肉到手电筒等几乎所有中国商品的商店，在城市大门打开之前很久就已经营业了。他们补充说，目前膨胀的南市人口中有五分之一在敌对行动后的两年里一直住在那里。既然繁荣似乎回来了，商店就备足了更多的货物。

page_data.en:
Tea House Remains
The world-famed Willow-Pattern
Tea House overlooked a stretch of
ruins on three sides.
A few Chinese were sipping tea
on its bottom floor when THE
CHINA PRESS representative visited
that ancient building, but the top
floor, which throughout the ages
served as meeting place for officials,
scholars, bon-vivants and curious
tourists from abroad, had its en-
trance barred.
The thousands of small fish
which used to inhabit the pond
around it have all died, the aged
genie of the place complained
sorrowfully, and one of the
boats, very much like the one
the famed Peet Li Po must
have used when he was drown-
ed while trying to reach for the
moon's reflection in the water,
was half-submerged in greenish
slime.
A serpentine Chinese stone
which, books say, has been a
landmark of the tea-house
since the Ming Dynasty, rose in
majestic loneliness out of twen-
tieth-century shambles.
Only in the large joss-house
where women used to pray for the
birth of sons, was the atmosphere
of the war pushed out altogether.
Miraculously, it had escaped bombs
and conflagration completely, and
the sound of human voices ring
through its courtyards and dim
vaulted halls.
page_data.zh:
茶馆犹存

世界闻名的柳纹茶馆（Willow-Pattern Tea House）三面俯瞰着一片废墟。
当《大美晚报》记者参观这座古老建筑时，几名中国人正在其底层品茶，但顶层——历代以来一直是官员、学者、享乐主义者和好奇的外国游客的聚会场所——入口已被封锁。
该地的老守护者悲伤地抱怨说，曾经栖息在周围池塘里的数千条小鱼都已死亡，其中一艘船非常像著名的李白（Peet Li Po，音译）在试图捞取水中月影时溺水所使用的船，半淹没在绿色的污泥中。
一块蛇形的中国石头，据书籍记载自明代以来一直是该茶馆的地标，在二十世纪的残垣断壁中庄严而孤独地耸立着。
只有在妇女曾经祈求生子的巨大庙宇中，战争的气氛才被完全驱散。奇迹般地，它完全避开了炸弹和火灾，人声在其庭院和昏暗的拱形大厅中回荡。

Subject. REPORTED NEGOTIATIONS BETWEEN MAYOR FU XIAO AN AND FRENCH AUTHORITIES FOR THE OPENING OF NANTAO.
Made by D.S.I. Maklaevsky Forwarded by C. ...

Information has been received to the effect that
informal negotiations have just begun between the
representatives of Mayor Fu Xiao An and the French
authorities on the subject of throwing open of Nantao
gates as a sequel of the proposed lifting of restrictions
governing residence in certain areas in Nantao bordering
on the French Concession.

The negotiations were started through the medium of
Mr. ..., a Frenchman, private secretary to Mr. D'Union
de Ruffe, a French lawyer of 25 Rue du Consulat.

It is also reported that a licence, to operate a
large gambling house in Nantao similar to that of the
Hollywood Gardens, Yu Yuen Road, has been granted by the
Japanese authorities to a group of Chinese gambling
promoters. The house would start operations as soon as
Nantao has been opened.

D.S.I. Maklaevsky

After the withdrawal of the Chinese forces
from the Shanghai area, the Japanese authorities took
over control of the Kaochongmiao Arsenal and Kiangnan
Dock at Nantao, and converted the arsenal into a
depot for military repairs also the smelting of iron
and copper for the Japanese Military. There are
some 1,000 Chinese employees under the supervision
of 200 Japanese employed in this work. The Kiangnan
Dock is known as the Shipbuilding Yard of the
Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha Ltd., where some 3,000 Chinese
artisans are employed supervised by 300 Japanese.
Apart from the repair of naval vessels and mercantile
shipping this dock also undertakes the building of
small boats.

Persons other than Japanese officials and
workers engaged in the two plants are prohibited from
entering the premises of the arsenal and the ship-
building yard, nor are they allowed to pass through
the military zone between Pan Soong Yuen Road and the
Si Pao Tan, Kaochongmiao, the Lunghua Aerodrome and
its vicinity and vicinity of Japanese billets. It is
learned that the residents of Nantao are experiencing
great inconvenience because of constant change and
removal of billets by the Japanese garrisons.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

主题：南市局势
由. 调查员潘连璧呈报 经. C. Giddons 转递

中国军队撤离上海地区后，日本当局接管了南市的高昌庙兵工厂和江南造船所，并将兵工厂改为日军维修仓库，同时也用于冶炼铁和铜供日军使用。约有1,000名中国雇员在此工作，受200名日本人监督。江南造船所现称为三菱商事株式会社造船厂，雇佣约3,000名中国工匠，受300名日本人监督。除修理海军舰艇和商船外，该造船厂还承建小型船只。

除日本官员及在上述两厂工作的工人外，其他人禁止进入兵工厂和造船厂区域，也不允许穿过潘松园路（Pan Soong Yuen Road）与泗宝滩、高昌庙、龙华机场及其周边地区以及日军营房附近之间的军事区。据悉，由于日军驻防部队频繁更换和搬迁营房，南市居民深感不便。

Subject Shen Sze Ching (沈世景), Chief of the Nantao Administrative
Office - departure for Japan.
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih, Forwarded by C. Crawford. A.S.

Shen Sze Ching, Chief of the Nantao Administra-
tive Office, left Nantao for Hongkew District by
motorcar via the French Bund at 8 a.m., October 13,
1939, for the purpose of boarding a steamer for Japan
on a mission of inspection. When leaving Nantao, he
was accompanied as far as the French Concession
Boundary, by some 70 members of the Nantao Branch of
the Greater Shanghai Youths' Corps and employees of
the Nantao Administrative Office.

Shen Sze Ching alias Shen Ngoh Kao (沈鶴皋),
aged 27, native of Shanghai, is a returned student
from France. He belongs to a wealthy family, his
grandfather being Shen Tse Hsien (沈志賢), owner of
the Pan Sung Yuan Garden in Nantao.

In view of Shen's departure, Tsu Wei Ming
(朱惠民), officer in charge of the second section
and also of the "Pao Chah" Section of the Nantao
Administrative Office, has been appointed by Mayor
Fu Siao En as acting chief of the Nantao Administrative
Office.

沈世景，又名沈鹤皋（Shen Ngoh Kao），27岁，上海人，留法归国学生。出身富裕家庭，其祖父为沈志贤（Shen Tse Hsien），系南市潘松园主人。

REPORT
Date October 13, 1939.

Subject Nantao Situation - issue of citizens' certificates and passes.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih. Forwarded by C. Crawford

During September, 1939, the Nantao
Administrative Office, 50 Ih Soh Ka, Nantao,
made an attempt to enforce the "Pao Chah" system
by issuing new citizens' certificates, while the
Japanese military at Nantao suspended the issuing
of passes and the Police Bureau in Nantao at the
same time stopped the issue of citizens' certifi-
cates. But the old certificates issued by the
Police Bureau are still in use.

During the morning of October 11, however,
the Japanese sentries at Sin Kai Ho (新開河),
Nantao, prohibited people from entering or leaving
Nantao without producing new citizens' certificates
issued by the Nantao Administrative Office. The
Japanese sentries at the Nantao Bund took the same
action on entrance by the Whangpoo River. As the
majority of the people are not in a position to
obtain new citizens' certificates, the Japanese
military later allowed the people to pass through
on the strength of the old certificates but issued
a circular to the effect that new certificates be
obtained before October 26, after which no persons valid
should be/allowed to enter or leave Nantao on
the old certificates.

A fee of 40 cents is charged by the Nantao
Administrative Office for each certificate issued.
Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D.C. ( Special Branch )

主题：南市局势 - 签发公民证和通行证。

由调查员潘连璧呈报。经克劳福德转递

1939年9月期间，位于南市一粟街50号的南市行政公署试图通过签发新的公民证来推行“保查”制度，而驻南市的日军暂停签发通行证，同时南市警察局也停止签发公民证。但警察局签发的旧证件仍在继续使用。

然而，10月11日上午，驻南市新开河（Sin Kai Ho）的日军哨兵禁止未出示南市行政公署签发的新公民证的人员进出南市。驻南市外滩的日军哨兵在黄浦江入口处也采取了同样行动。由于大多数民众无法获得新公民证，日军后来允许民众凭旧证件通行，但发布通告称须在10月26日前取得新证件，此后任何人不得凭旧证件进出南市。

南市行政公署对每张签发的证件收取40美分费用。

Between 6 a.m. and 11 a.m., 6.10.39, the
transportation service between Pootung and Nan Ma Tao,
Nantao, was suspended due to 500 Japanese soliders
disembarking at Nan Ma Tao. The 500 soliders are to be
accommodated at Hu Chun Yin (軍營), Kao Chang
Miao (高昌廟) and Lunghwa Road respectively.
The boundary between the French Concession and
Nantao (Boulevard des de Republiques) has been marked
by the Japanese authorities as a "forbidden" zone and
people are prohibited from entering and loitering there.
The Japanese military have had considerable
trouble removing people from this area and between 7 a.m.
and 6 p.m., 6.10.39, barb-wire and wooden obstructions
were
have been placed along the roadway at the building line

法租界与南市之间的边界（共和大道 Boulevard des de Republiques）已被日本当局标记为“禁区”，禁止人们进入和在该处逗留。
日军在将该区域人员迁出方面遇到了相当大的困难，1939年10月6日上午7时至下午6时之间，沿建筑线的道路上设置了铁丝网和木制障碍物，以防止共和大道的居民进入该区域。

Huang, Tao Kang (黃寶康), head of the
Tung Chong Road Guild (東昌路公所), Pootung,
under the control of the Pootung District Adminis-
trative Office, was arrested by the Japanese
Gendarmerie in the offices of the Guild situated in
the New Pootung Alleyway (新浦東里), Shan Tang
Road (善堂路), Pootung, at about 5 p.m. on
September 14, 1939. His arrest is due to a report
received by the Japanese Gendarmerie to the effect
that at the end of August 1939, he detained three
boats from Sungkiang in the Whangpoo River and
seized therefrom 300 "zors" of rice under the pretext
of relieving the rice situation in Pootung. He
subsequently sold the rice but failed to pay the
owners of the rice.
Huang, aged around 36 or 37, is the pro-
prietor of the Huang Liang Kee (黃增記) Rice Shop,
Yang Kia Doo (楊家渡), Pootung. Following the
withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai at the end
of 1937, he organized the Tung Chong Road Maintenance
Association (東昌路維持會) and made himself the
Chairman. The association was later abolished by the
Pootung District Administrative Office and he was
then appointed Head of the Tung Chong Road Guild,
which position he held up to the time of his arrest.

Pan Lien-pik
D. I.

Nantao and Pootung will be issued by the respective
administrative offices who have received blank passes

colour and valid for two months, after which period new

Date July 31, 1939.
Subject Reopening of the Wen Miao Temple, City
Made by J.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Giaton

The Wen Miao Temple ( 文廟 ), also known
as the "Mass Education Institute" ( 民衆教育館 ),
222 Wen Miao Road, City, entrance to which has been
prohibited ever since the Japanese occupation of
Nantao at the end of 1937, has been reopened to the
public between the hours of 7 a.m. and 5 p.m., daily
from July 26, 1939. No admission charge is
required.

The temple is now renamed the Confucius Temple
( 夫子廟 ) and all images of ancient Chinese
saints, sages, philosophers and other men of learning
have been carefully preserved but the portraits of
the 72 martyrs and those of the famous Chinese
military figures and patriots of ancient times have
been totally removed. The numerous inscriptions
appertaining to the educational principles of the
Kuomintang which formerly adorned the premises, have
now been either destroyed or removed. The Nantao
District Administrative Office has posted all over
the place such slogans as "Cease hostilities and
advocate peace", "Establish a New Order in the Orient",
"Sino-Japanese cooperation", "Down with the Chiang
Regime" and "Annihilate the Communist Party".

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

文庙（Wen Miao Temple），又称“民众教育馆”，位于城内文庙路222号，自1937年底日军占领南市以来入口一直被禁止，现自1939年7月26日起，每日上午7时至下午5时重新对公众开放。无需门票。

该庙现已更名为夫子庙（Confucius Temple），所有中国古代圣贤、哲学家及其他学者的塑像均得到妥善保存，但72烈士的肖像以及古代著名中国军事人物和爱国者的肖像已被全部移除。以前装饰在该处的许多关于国民党教育原则的题词，现已被销毁或移除。南区行政公署在各处张贴了诸如“停止敌对行动，倡导和平”、“建立东亚新秩序”、“中日合作”、“打倒蒋政权”和“剿灭共产党”等标语。

潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）

Nantao.
Made by....................    Forwarded by....................

At 3.40 p.m., May 25, an explosion of
tremendous force occurred on the former site of
the Kiangnan Arsenal, Kao Chong Miao, Nantao,
reported to have been caused through carelessness
on the part of Japanese soldiers and Chinese
coolies engaged in removing quantities of explosives.
The premises in which the explosives were stored
were demolished, and some 5 Japanese soldiers and
5 Chinese coolies are reported to have been killed
while 13 Japanese soldiers and more than 10 Chinese
coolies were injured. After the explosion the
Japanese threw a cordon around the scene, and detailed
particulars of the accident are therefore unavailable.

Certified true copy.
H. C. Hardley

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAY 26 1939

Old Bomb Explodes in
Kiangnan Area

Sensation Created as Many
Houses Are Shaken

A terrific explosion of a bomb or
mine occurred in Nantao yesterday
shortly before 4 p.m., shaking windows
of buildings in the French concession
near the border of the native city and
causing curiosity among many people
who bombarded newspaper offices
with telephone calls for information.
Although it was hard to ascertain the
cause of the explosion and the extent
of damage done, if any, it was
generally believed that it was ac-
cidental.
Those who were in offices and many
housewives, too, were aroused by the
explosion and they exchanged tele-
phone calls telling of what they
heard. It was suggested that the
Japanese might be engaged in blasting
away the boom across the Whangpoo
erected by Chinese authorities in
Nantao before they withdrew and that
the explosion occurred in Lunghwa
where a Japanese magazine is located.
These reports, however, were later
discredited when information grad-
ually leaked out from other sources.
Probably the most reliable solution to
the mystery could only be offered by
the Japanese because the explosion
occurred in the occupied area, but at
last night's press conference the
Japanese spokesman gave no details,
belittling its importance, asserting that
it might be an explosion of a missile
in the industrial section near the
former Kiangnan Arsenal.
A Chinese news agency which had
made investigation stated last night
that the explosion was that of a big
bomb left behind by Chinese forces in
Nantao. It occurred in Lu Bon Road
but no details were given.

（批：The Rays）
（批：E dy 5）
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年5月26日

江南地区旧炸弹爆炸

多所房屋震动引起轰动

昨天下午4点前不久，南市发生了一起炸弹或地雷的巨大爆炸，震动了靠近华界边境的法租界建筑物的窗户，引起许多人的好奇，他们纷纷打电话给报社询问信息。虽然很难确定爆炸的原因和造成的损坏程度（如果有的话），但人们普遍认为这是意外事故。
那些在办公室里的人和许多家庭主妇也被爆炸惊醒，他们互相通电话，讲述他们听到的情况。有人推测，日本人可能正在爆破中国当局在撤退前于南市黄浦江上设置的封锁线，并且爆炸发生在龙华，那里有一个日本军火库。然而，随着其他来源的消息逐渐泄露，这些报道后来被证实不可信。也许只有日本人才能提供最可靠的谜底解释，因为爆炸发生在占领区，但在昨晚的新闻发布会上，日本发言人没有提供细节，轻视其重要性，声称这可能是前江南制造局附近工业区的一枚导弹爆炸。
一家进行过调查的中国通讯社昨晚称，爆炸是中国军队留在南市的巨型炸弹引起的。爆炸发生在鲁班路，但未提供细节。

（批注：The Rays）
（批注：E dy 5）

13657
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
MAY 26 1932
Fire Rages in Nantao
A big fire had been burning in
Nantao since late yesterday after-
noon and it still could be seen late
last night. A check with various
sources revealed that there was a
fire, but none seemed to know where
it was and how it started. One Chi-
nese source stated that the conflagra-
tion occurred in the Kaochangmiao
area in Nantao which was described
as an industrial section of the native
city by the Japanese spokesman,
and if it was true then the fire
might have something to do with
the explosion which shook the town
in the afternoon. The explosion is
therefore further mystified by the
fire.

《字林西报》。
1932年5月26日
南市大火
自昨天下午晚些时候起，南市一直发生大火，直到昨晚深夜仍可见火光。经多方核实，确实发生了火灾，但似乎无人知晓火灾地点及起因。一位中方消息人士称，火灾发生在南市高昌庙地区，日本发言人将该地区描述为华界的工业区，如果属实，那么火灾可能与下午震动全镇的爆炸有关。因此，火灾使爆炸事件更加神秘。

Japanese Special Service Section in Nantao (corner
of Boon Lai Road and Ih Soh Ka), accompanied by
five Chinese detectives of the Police Bureau of the

Subject Nantao Situation

Made by. D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by. C. Crawford

（印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE * 13 MAY 1939）

With a view to suppressing the anti-Japanese feelings of the people now living in Nantao and City, a number of members of the Japanese Military Police, disguised as Chinese, have been keeping observation in busy parts of the district. These persons, clad in Chinese clothing (mostly blue cotton cloth jacket and pants) mingle with crowds of Chinese in food and tea shops and pay attention to conversation among them. Should they discover any persons discussing the war situation or criticizing the administration of the Japanese authorities, they arrest them.

On May 10 and 11, 1939, some twenty persons are said to have been arrested in this manner. They are now detained at the Nantao Branch Headquarters of the Japanese Military Police, Boon Lai Road, pending investigations. Those who are found to have been connected with anti-Japanese activities will be handed over to the Main Headquarters of Japanese Military Police at Lunghwa for disposal.

SHANGHAI TIMES.
MAR 2 4 1939

USEFUL WORK FOUND
FOR REFUGEES
“Goodwill Industries”
Providing Training
For Destitute

Among the relief organizations to cheer the lives of the real and partially destitute refugees is the work of the “Goodwill Industries,” where several hundred homeless and unemployed have secured light work, food, clothing, cash wages and vocational training. A few important points which will give one idea of the work they are doing in making it possible for war sufferers to make a new start in life, are outlined below:
“Goodwill Industries” acts as a collecting and distributing agency in assisting persons who have things to be disposed of in placing these directly into the hands of the genuinely needy.
Employment has been given in many trades as in sewing rooms, washing and dyeing-rooms, shoemaking, basket-making, carpentry, knitting, mop-making, hat-making, gardening etc., with payment in food, clothing, and cash on the refugee camp basis.
“Goodwill Industries” provides labour with free clinics to take care of the health of workers, children and neighbourhood people. This work has helped thousands of refugees to lessen the ills of the unfortunates and has improved their health conditions.
In order to educate the illiterate in those devastated areas, free schools and kindergartens are being conducted for the children of working mothers and the poor people around the Centre.
The “Goodwill” provides labour in garden work in the yard of their Mission Schools. A part of the refugees helped plant vegetables, such as lettuce and other things.
In short, the “Goodwill Industries” is doing splendid relief work in and beyond the Nantao Refugee Zone with a programme of self-help reclamation which is carried on in the spirit of Christian Service. Telephone 16082 or write “Goodwill Industries,” 115 Hankow Road, Shanghai, and money and other contributions will be called for at your convenience.

（印：POLICE REGISTRY No. S.-b. 1 Date）
（批：R 24/3）

《字林西报》。
1939年3月24日

为难民找到有益的工作
“善导工业社”
为贫困者提供培训

在众多旨在改善真正贫困及部分贫困难民生活的救济组织中，“善导工业社”（Goodwill Industries）的工作值得一提，数百名无家可归和失业者在此获得了轻体力工作、食物、衣物、现金工资和职业培训。以下是其工作要点概述，从中可窥见他们如何帮助战争受害者重新开始生活：
“善导工业社”作为一个收集和分发机构，协助拥有待处理物品的人将这些物品直接送到真正有需要的人手中。
在许多行业提供了就业机会，如缝纫室、洗衣染坊、制鞋、编织篮子、木工、针织、制作拖把、制帽、园艺等，报酬以难民营标准的食物、衣物和现金支付。
“善导工业社”为劳工提供免费诊所，以照顾工人、儿童和邻里居民的健康。这项工作帮助成千上万的难民减轻了不幸者的病痛，改善了他们的健康状况。
为了教育受灾地区的文盲，为中心周围工作的母亲的孩子和穷人开办了免费学校和幼儿园。
“善导”在其教会学校的院子里提供园艺劳动岗位。部分难民帮助种植蔬菜，如生菜和其他作物。
总之，“善导工业社”在南市难民区内及周边地区开展了出色的救济工作，其自力更生的复兴计划秉承基督教服务精神开展。电话16082或写信至“善导工业社”，地址：上海汉口路115号，我们将根据您的方便上门收取捐款及其他物资。

（印章：警务处登记处 编号 S.-b. 1 日期）

Date January 24, 1939.

Subject Present situation in Nantao

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Crawford.

On January 22 and 23, 1939, about 50 male Chinese of the coolie class living in the Nantao Refugee Zone were pressed into service by the Japanese soldiers of the Nantao Garrison billeted in the Wan Tso Primary School, Wan Tso Street, City. These coolies were put to work during the day constructing machine gun nests and other defence works around the school while at night they were herded into the school premises and detained there.

On January 22, 1939, some 30 soldiers of the Japanese Gendarmerie stationed in the premises of the former Police Bureau on Hoon Lai Road, Nantao, were replaced by another company of equal strength who are reported to have arrived from Soochow.

It is reported that the former site of the Police Bureau on Boon Lai Road, Nantao, will be reoccupied by the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government under Loo Ying (盧英), at present located in the Civic Centre, Kiangwan.

Aid for Refugees.
The Chinese Pharmacies' Association yesterday
despatched circulars to its members, inviting them to
reserve monthly from November, 5% of their business
profits for helping refugees. This scheme is to last for
6 months. Employees will also contribute 1% of their
monthly wages to this movement.
The Shanghai Restaurants' Association has decided to
collect as from November 1 in all local restaurants a
"poor tax" amounting to 5% of customers' bills.
The Hotels' Association will collect, from November

collected in all local hotels.
The Cigarette & Exchange Shops Association will
collect from November, a "poor tax" of $1 per case of
cigarettes purchased by its members.

Subject (in full)...Situation in Nantao - explosion of handgrenade.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. [Signature]

At 12.30 p.m., September 15, a handgrenade exploded
in an alleyway behind the Ming Lih (民立) Girls' Middle
School, Wen Miao Road (文庙路), Nantao. No persons
were injured, and no arrests were made by the Japanese
military who conducted a search of the dwelling houses in
the vicinity following the explosion. A bamboo basket
and an iron hook, evidently the property of a rag picker,
were found on the scene, and from this it would appear
that the explosion was caused by a rag picker searching a
pile of garbage in which the missile was reposing.

REPORT    Date...June.17,......19 38.

Subject.... Situation in Nantao.

Made by. D.I. Pan Lien-pih    Forwarded by. C. Crawford L.J.

Considering that the situation in Nantao did not
warrant the continued existence of the Pacification Section
situated at the corner of Boon Lai Road and Ih Soh Ka, Nantao,
the Japanese military authorities ordered its closure on
June 13, 1938 and the establishment of a special service
section of the Japanese Military Forces for Nantao. The
special service section was organized and staffed with the
same personnel as the Pacification Section, and commenced
to operate on June 13. The special service section will
have under its control the "Nantao Autonomous Commission"
as did the Pacification Section, leaving the supervision
of all Nantao organs attached to the "Shanghai Municipal
Administrative Office" in the hands of the Japanese
advisors appointed.

The Japanese Forces have taken further districts in
the Nantao area into the prohibited area and in consequence
refugees sheltering in that areas have been removed and
have taken up residence in the Nantao Safety Zone. According
to the Nantao Head Office of the International Relief
Committee, approximately 23,000 have entered the Nantao
Safety Zone and been accommodated in refugee camps established
by the Committee. The number of refugees supported by the
Committee in the Safety Zone now totals 65,000.

The water supply for residents in the Nantao Safety
Zone was restored on June 10, but no electricity is supplied
except that to Japanese military establishments.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 17 JUNE 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

主题.... 南市局势。

制作人. 侦探长潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）    转呈人. C. Crawford L.J.

鉴于南市局势已不再需要继续存在位于南市蓬莱路与一粟街拐角处的绥靖科，日本军方当局于1938年6月13日下令将其关闭，并成立日本军队南市特务科。该特务科由与绥靖科相同的人员组织和配备，并于6月13日开始运作。特务科将像绥靖科一样控制“南市自治委员会”，而将所有隶属于“上海市政公署”的南市机构的监督权留在任命的日本顾问手中。

日军已将南市地区的更多街区划入禁区，因此，避难在该地区的难民已被撤离，并迁入南市安全区居住。据国际救济委员会南市总办事处称，约有23,000人进入南市安全区，并被安置在该委员会建立的难民营中。目前由该委员会在安全区供养的难民总数已达65,000人。

南市安全区居民的供水已于6月10日恢复，但除供应日本军事设施外，不供应电力。

Subject Situation in Nantao.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford W.S.

The population of the Nantao Safety Zone now consists
of 242,000, of whom 80,000 earn their own living, 22,000
live in refugee camps, 20,000 live in their own homes but
are supported by the International Relief Committee; the
remaining 120,000 recently moved in from other divisions
of Nantao as a result of the designation of the district
south of Loh Ka Pang Road as a forbidden area by the Japanese
military.

After the dissolution of the Nantao Traders' Association
by the Industrial and Commercial Section of the "Nantao
Autonomous Commission" on April 11, 1938 (vide Special Branch
report dated April 12, 1938 on the arrest of refugees in
the Nantao Safety Zone), Mr. Chow Zung Fu (周潤甫),
Chief of the Industrial and Commercial Section, applied
many times for the issue of a few passes to facilitate
transportation of commodities from the French Concession
to the Nantao Safety Zone, but the French authorities rejected
his applications on the assumption that the organization is
sponsored by the Japanese. Alarmed by a phenomenal increase
in the population in the Nantao Safety Zone and fearing
the consequence of a shortage in daily necessities, the
Japanese military are said to have asked a certain German
to approach Mr. Sung Sing Fu (沈心撫), chairman of the
now defunct Nantao Traders' Association, who resides with
his family in Room 263, Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, with
a proposal that the Nantao Traders' Association be resuscitated
and that he be re-appointed head of the organization with
the German acting as advisor. The Japanese took this action

The "Nantao Autonomous Commission" on March 22nd, issued a notification stating that the owners of land under cultivation, which is situated in the vicinity of Lunghwa Road and Kong Chu Road, Nantao, must register with the Commission before March 28th, and that should they fail to register within the stipulated period, their land will be confiscated and would eventually be given to the farmers who could show a good results of their labour.

On March 26th, the Autonomous Commission issued another notification stating that land owners who were in possession of title deeds issued by the Land Bureau of the Shanghai City Government must exchange these for documents issued by the Autonomous Commission and pay fees according to the following scale:-

1) .001 of the value of land on which no houses are built or upon which the houses have been destroyed.
2) .002 of the value of land on which the houses are intact.

On March 23rd, Mr. Pan Tse-chieh (潘志傑), former director of the Nantao Head Office of the International Relief Committee, 235 Fang Pang Road, Nantao, who resigned from his office on February 24th, as the result of a difference with the Japanese Military in Nantao, returned to his post on being persuaded to do so by Father Jacquinot. Date March 7, 1938.
Subject Dissension between the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" and the
Police Bureau of the "Dah Dao City Government."
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Dissension now exists between the "Nantao Autonomous
Commission" and the Police Bureau of the "Dah Dao City
Government" over the question of administrative power.
Recently the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" enforced
the registration of families and the obtaining of "law-
abiding citizen" certificates by residents. The administration
also established a market at West Gate and recruited 2,000
scavengers. A uniformed police force was also formed.
These innovations were considered by the Police Bureau of the
"Dah Dao City Government" to encroach upon the functions
of the Nantao Branch Bureau. A petition requesting the
suppression of these reforms by the "Nantao Autonomous
Commission" was therefore submitted by the Police Bureau
to the "Dah Dao City Government," and a consultation was
held between the authorities of the City Government and Mr.
Nishimura (西村), who serves as advisor to the "Dah Dao
City Government" and concurrently acts as the sponsor of the
"Nantao Autonomous Commission." Mr. Nishimura counselled
cooperation between the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" and
the "Dah Dao City Government" Police Bureau, but members
of the Autonomous Commission refused to agree to a compromise
and insisted on being permitted to exercise to the full such
powers of administration as are ordinarily vested in an
autonomous administration.
Up to the present the dispute remains unsettled.

日期：1938年3月7日。
主题：“南市自治委员会”与“大道市政府”警察局之间的分歧。
由督察员潘连璧呈报，经副警司 C. Crawford 转呈。

目前，“南市自治委员会”与“大道市政府”警察局之间因行政权力问题存在分歧。最近，“南市自治委员会”强制推行家庭登记，并要求居民领取“守法公民”证。该行政机构还在西门设立了一个市场，并招募了2,000名清道夫。此外还组建了一支着装警察部队。“大道市政府”警察局认为这些新举措侵犯了南市分局的职能。因此，警察局向“大道市政府”提交了一份请愿书，要求制止“南市自治委员会”的这些改革措施；市政府当局与担任“大道市政府”顾问兼“南市自治委员会”赞助人的西村（Nishimura）先生进行了磋商。西村先生建议“南市自治委员会”与“大道市政府”警察局合作，但自治委员会成员拒绝妥协，坚持要求被允许充分行使通常属于自治行政机构的行政权力。
截至目前，争端仍未解决。

March 4, 1938.

Shanghai Mainichi

THE STATUS QUO IN NANTAO

Since the organization of an Autonomous
Committee in Nantao on January 11, the Pacification Section
of the Japanese Army experienced many difficulties and
were kept exceedingly busy.
On November 13, 1937, work was begun on the
ruins. Accommodation and food had to be found for
refugees. A medical section was formed to co-operate
with the medical department of the army. To assure peace
in the district a Police Force of 350 men was organized
and kept in touch with the Japanese Gendarmes. Thus, an
Autonomous Committee was formed in Nantao.
To procure funds the Autonomous Committee
commenced a ferry service between Nantao and Pootung. On
the first day, January 9, only 15 sen was collected, but on
the following day, the takings amounted to Yen 27.34. At
present about Yen 300 are taken in daily. It forms a
reliable source of revenue to the Committee.
The Autonomous Committee has four departments,
namely, the General Affairs Department, the Finance
Department, the Rehabilitation Department and the Public
Works Department. The Rehabilitation Department deals
principally with the cleaning of streets. 500 to 600
coolies are employed daily under the supervision of four
Japanese. The Public Works Department issues certificates
of Good Citizenship and is responsible for the census.
On the first day 133 certificates were issued and 58
families were registered. The following day, 564
certificates were issued and 298 families registered. On
the 25th day, 753 certificates were issued and 347 families
registered. On the 26th day, so many applicants had
called that 15 clerks were unable to dispose of the work.
The certificates are issued at a fee of 5 sen each.
Thus, a sum of Yen 1,500 monthly is received by the Public
Welfare Department.
The General Affairs Department handles
proclamations etc. At the request of other departments,
the Finance Department distributes money among other
departments. Public works such as public ricshas,
buses, electric supply and waterworks are now under
consideration.
The First Hsi Hua Primary School was
established by the Public Welfare Department on February 5
with four teachers.
It is generally believed that Sino-Japanese
relations can be improved through the education of the
children. A similar school will be opened soon in the
refugee zone. All the stationery used by the school
children is supplied by the Committee. 90% of the 120
school children attend school regularly. A market has
also been established by the Committee. Retail prices
are fixed by the Committee.
The establishment of a Citizens Bank is
also under consideration by the Committee.

（右上角批注：RECD D. 8155B 5 3 38）

1938年3月4日。

《上海每日新闻》

南市现状

自1月11日南市成立自治委员会以来，日军绥靖部门遇到了许多困难，工作极为繁忙。
1937年11月13日，废墟清理工作开始。必须为难民寻找住所和食物。成立了医疗部门以配合军队医疗部门工作。为确保该地区和平，组建了一支350人的警察部队，并与日本宪兵队保持联系。由此，南市成立了自治委员会。
为了筹集资金，自治委员会开通了南市与浦东之间的轮渡服务。第一天，即1月9日，仅收取了15钱（sen），但第二天，收入达到27.34日元。目前每天收入约300日元。这成为委员会可靠的收入来源。
自治委员会下设四个部门，即总务部、财政部、复兴部和工程部。复兴部主要负责街道清洁工作。在四名日本人的监督下，每天雇用500至600名苦力。工程部负责发放“良民证”并负责人口普查。第一天发放了133张证书，登记了58个家庭。第二天，发放了564张证书，登记了298个家庭。第25天，发放了753张证书，登记了347个家庭。第26天，申请人太多，15名职员无法处理完所有工作。每张证书收费5钱。因此，社会福利部每月可获得1,500日元的收入。
总务部负责处理公告等事务。应其他部门的要求，财政部向其他部门分配资金。目前正在考虑公共交通人力车、公共汽车、电力供应和自来水等公共工程事项。
第一西华小学由社会福利部于2月5日成立，配有四名教师。
人们普遍认为，通过儿童教育可以改善中日关系。难民区不久也将开设一所类似的学校。学生使用的所有文具均由委员会提供。120名学生中有90%定期上学。委员会还建立了一个市场。零售价格由委员会规定。
委员会也在考虑建立一家市民银行。

（右上角批注：RECD D. 8155B 5 3 38）

page_data.en:
March 4, 1938. - 2-

The above is a brief report of the activities
undertaken in Nantao. The populace are contented.
The intellectual and wealthy Chinese refugees in French
Concession or Settlement are returning to their homes in
Nantao. One reason of this is probably due to the
difficulty of passing from the French Concession into
Nantao. Another reason is the damage done to their
homes and factories. All former residents of Nantao
should return to their old homes immediately and co-operate
with the Autonomous Committee in building a prosperous
Nantao. The Japanese Military Authorities will protect
their life and property.

MANOEUVRES OF THE SETTLEMENT GUARDING UNIT

Large scale manoeuvres will be carried out
by the Settlement Guarding Unit, a detachment of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, in Hongkew and Yangtsepoo
districts on the early morning of March 5. No
restrictions will be placed on traffic whilst the
manoeuvres are going on.

RICSHA PULLERS WILL BE ALLOWED IN THE NORTHERN AREA

The Settlement Guarding Unit has decided
to permit the operation of ricsha pullers in the area.
The Gendarmerie and the Japanese Consular Police are
discussing the measures to be adopted. No decision
has yet been made officially, for the admittance of a
large number of ricsha pullers into the area may affect
peace and order in the area. It is reported that the
authorities will allow one Japanese and two Formosan
ricsha owners to make the necessary preparations, and that
a special rate of fares which will have no connection
with that of the southern area will be set up.

S.S. "SHANGHAI MARU" ARRIVES HERE ON MARCH 3

The s.s. "Shanghai Maru" arrived here from
Nagasaki with 400 passengers at 1 p.m. March 3 and berthed
at the N.Y.K. Wayside Wharf, Yangtsepoo Road. Among
the passengers was a party of ten representatives of
various circles in Saga Prefecture.
page_data.zh:
1938年3月4日。 - 2-

以上是关于南市所开展活动的简要报告。民众感到满意。
居住在法租界或公共租界的知识分子和富裕的中国难民正在返回他们在南市的家园。其中一个原因可能是从法租界进入南市存在困难。另一个原因是他们的家园和工厂遭受了破坏。所有南市前居民应立即返回旧居，并与自治委员会合作，建设繁荣的南市。日本军方将保护他们的生命和财产。

租界守备队演习

日本海军陆战队分遣队下属的租界守备队将于3月5日凌晨在虹口和杨浦区进行大规模演习。演习期间交通不受限制。

北区将允许人力车夫运营

租界守备队已决定允许在该区域运营人力车。宪兵队和日本领事警察正在讨论拟采取的措施。由于大量人力车夫进入该区域可能会影响当地的治安秩序，官方尚未做出决定。据报道，当局将允许一名日本人和两名台湾籍人力车车主进行必要准备，并将制定与南区费率无关的特殊费率。

“上海丸”轮船于3月3日抵达此处

“上海丸”轮船于3月3日下午1点从长崎载着400名乘客抵达此处，停靠在杨树浦路日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）路边码头。乘客中包括佐贺县各界代表十人组成的代表团。

Subject "Nantao Autonomous Commission" - activities.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C Casford D.I.

The number of persons attached to the "Mobile Police Force" which is under the control of the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" situated at 50 Ih Soh Ka, Boon Lai Road, Nantao, was recently increased to two hundred, and its headquarters removed from the Mohammedan Church on Foh Yeu Road to the premises of the "Nantao Autonomous Commission," 50 Ih Soh Ka, Boon Lai Road. These policemen, who have been chosen from among Nantao refugees and whose duties are to maintain peace and order in the Nantao Safety Zone, are paid no wages but are provided with free board and lodging. Fifty of the 200 members are dressed in uniforms similar to those worn by members of the Police Bureau of the "Dah Dao City Government." The only difference between the uniforms worn by these volunteers and those adopted by the Police Bureau is in the colour of the band around the cap, the colour on the caps of the volunteers being white, while that on the caps of members of the Police Bureau is yellow. Another distinguishing mark on the uniforms of those volunteers is a white strip on the sleeves of their tunics.

On February 23, the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" commenced to issue "law abiding citizen" certificates to residents who possess residence passes. Every resident over the age of 16 is required to apply for a "law abiding citizen" certificate, for which five cents has to be paid and which must be carried on the person. About one hundred and fifty families consisting of 500 persons have applied and obtained these "law abiding citizen" certificates.

由督察员潘连璧呈报，经督察员 C Casford 转呈。

隶属于位于南市蓬莱路（Boon Lai Road）伊索街（Ih Soh Ka，音译）50号的“南市自治委员会”管辖下的“流动警察部队”的人数最近增加到两百人，其总部也从佛佑路（Foh Yeu Road，音译）的清真寺迁至南市蓬莱路伊索街50号的“南市自治委员会”办公处。这些警察是从南市难民中挑选出来的，职责是维持南市安全区的和平与秩序，他们不领取工资，但提供免费食宿。这200名成员中有50人身着与“大道市政府”警察局成员相似的制服。这些志愿者所穿制服与警察局采用的制服之间的唯一区别在于帽带的颜色，志愿者帽子上的颜色为白色，而警察局成员帽子上的颜色为黄色。这些志愿者制服的另一个显著标志是其上衣袖子上有一条白色条纹。

Translation of Despatch No.2 to Council from
Shanghai Nantao Self-Government Committee.
Dated 19th January, 1938.

Manifesto: Copy forwarded.

When the recent local hostilities spread to Nantao, residents
in that district fled in all directions, and they are in a
miserable plight. Fortunately, the fighting moved westward, and
conditions in this city are gradually being readjusted. It is
understandable for the former business men and residents of Nantao
to stay away indefinitely from their business and home. Above
all, it is necessary that there should be somebody to maintain
peace and good order in that district.

This Committee was established on 11th January. The Chinese
and foreign communities should both sympathize with its difficulties.
The Council has always been concerned with the situation in Chinese
territory. A manifesto issued by the Committee is enclosed
herewith. It is hoped that a spirit of friendship and co-operation
will develop between the Council and the Committee, and that the
said district will be rehabilitated within the shortest time
possible.

(Chopped & Signed) Zong Yulin, Chairman,
Nantao Self-Government Committee
Ling Chi-teh, Vice-Chairman

Incl: Manifesto

近期本地战事蔓延至南市，该区居民四散奔逃，处境凄惨。幸而战事向西转移，本市局势正逐渐调整恢复。原南市商界人士及居民无限期远离其产业与家园，实属情有可原。最重要的是，该区须有人维持和平与良好秩序。

本委员会于1月11日成立。中外各界应对其困难予以同情。工部局一向关注华界局势。兹附上本委员会发布的宣言一份。期望工部局与本委员会之间能发展出友好合作的精神，并使该区在最短时间内得以复兴。

Translation of enclosure
Manifesto of the Shanghai Nantao
Self-Government Committee.

Shanghai is a big commercial port visited by many sea-going
vessels and connected with a large volume of vehicular traffic.
Its streets are lined with houses and crowded with business people.
Without taking into consideration its foreign population, there are
several millions of Chinese who live, move and have their being in
this city. A great misfortune has now befallen this city.
A disastrous war has reduced to ashes countless human habitations.
What have the innocent people done that they should be deprived of
their homes and driven from one place to another? The aged, with
nowhere to find shelter, are left to suffer the rigours of weather,
while small children are cruelly separated from their parents.
To prevent such refugees from dying of starvation local residents
have been obliged to establish camps for them and to devise measures
for supplying them with food and clothing. Nevertheless, as the
number to be cared for is far in excess of the resources at our
command, our heart sinks in contemplating the difficulty of affording
adequate relief. Should the present state of affairs continue
unchanged and no effort be made to co-ordinate the work of mutual
assistance, it will be inconceivable what may happen to public safety
As the stability of a country depends largely on good order among
her people, it is impossible to restore normal conditions in this
city without first reestablishing peace and order among the local
residents.

Moreover, for several thousand years, as history informs us,
China has been a nation which prides herself on the propriety and
education of her people, which sets a high value on benevolence and
righteousness and which prefers the pursuit of peaceful culture to
self-aggrandizement through military might. In her administration she
showed a preference for the ways of a merciful Emperor to government
by force, and the inculcated filial piety and loyalty. These estab-
lished principles of the ancients have however been totally forgotten

上海是一个大型商业港口，海轮往来频繁，陆路交通繁忙。街道两旁房屋林立，商贾云集。若不计算外籍人口，亦有数百万中国人在此城市生活、活动及生存。如今这座城市遭遇了巨大的不幸。灾难性的战争将无数人居化为灰烬。无辜百姓何罪之有，竟致失去家园，流离失所？老者无处栖身，饱受风霜之苦；幼童与父母残酷分离。为防止此类难民饿死，当地居民被迫设立收容营，并设法供应衣食。然而，由于需照顾的人数远超我们所能支配的资源，想到难以提供充分救济，令人心沉。若现状持续不变，且不努力协调互助工作，公共安全将面临不可想象的后果。
鉴于国家的稳定很大程度上取决于人民的良序，若不首先恢复当地居民的和平与秩序，便不可能恢复本市的正常状态。

此外，据历史记载，数千年来，中国一直是一个以人民礼教为荣、高度重视仁义、偏好追求和平文化而非通过武力自大的国家。在治理上，她倾向于仁慈君主的治国之道，而非强力统治，并灌输孝道与忠诚。然而，这些古圣先贤确立的原则却在近代被完全遗忘

in recent times. The more our laws are modernized, the greater
became the complication in legislation. The people have no
longer any peace and are daily becoming more impoverished.
For the reconstruction and rehabilitation of this city we
have undertaken the difficult task of organizing this Committee.
Our objects are to remove all prejudices, settle all disputes,
restore peace to the survivors of the catastrophe, revive
business, promote personal equality and lay the foundation for
a lasting peace. It shall be our duty to eradicate all elements
tending to jeopardize international amity and to disturb the
mind of the people, as well as such evil habits as have been
acquired by the citizens. Therefore, we hope farmers will once
more be able to till their land, labourers to return to their
work, merchants to resume business and students to pursue
their studies. The revival of Shanghai will mean also the
resurrection of China. All our compatriots please pay attention
to this manifesto!

为了重建和复兴本市，我们承担了组织本委员会的艰巨任务。我们的目标是消除一切偏见，解决所有争端，为灾难幸存者恢复和平，振兴商业，促进人格平等，并为持久和平奠定基础。我们有责任铲除一切危及国际友谊、扰乱民心以及市民养成的恶习的因素。因此，我们希望农民能再次耕种土地，工人能重返工作岗位，商人能恢复营业，学生能继续学业。上海的复兴也意味着中国的重生。请全体同胞注意此宣言！

ONOMOUS COMMISSION IN NANTAO

Two months after the occupation of Nantao by Japanese troops, an autonomous commission was established in Nantao yesterday afternoon, with Mr. Chen Yun as chairman. Upper photo shows Mr. Chen making his inaugural address. On his left is an interpreter translating his speech into Japanese. Following the ceremony which was held in a primary school on Fenglai Road, the officials of the commission and Japanese officers were photographed, as shown in the lower photograph. [Domei.

Autonomous Commission Is Established In Nantao

Inaugural Ceremony With Certain Pomp Marks Opening Of New Administration; Created To End Privation And Usher In Peaceful Era

Exactly two months after the occupation of Nantao by Japanese troops, an autonomous commission was formally brought into existence in the Native City at 1 o'clock yesterday afternoon.

The inaugural ceremony, marked by solemnity and even pomp, was held at the Sicheng Primary School, Fenglai Road, Nantao.

Headed by Mr. Chen Yun, Chairman, and Mr. Ling Chi-tan, Vice-Chairman, the new Nantao governing body consists of 13 members.

In a manifesto read at the ceremony, Mr. Chen said his commission was created "to end privation caused by war and to help peaceful residents to pursue their daily tasks in happiness and prosperity."

The new organ, the manifesto said, will act as "the seed of a brighter future in Central China by freeing the people from the ... upon them by ...

ment of perpetual peace in the Oriental and its desire to co-operate with similar bodies in China.

Mr. Chen, a graduate of a law school, once served as deputy chief of the Public Safety Bureau's administrative section. He was also reported to be a member of the local Lawyers' Association.

Mr. Ling, who received his education in Japan, was described as a "shipping magnate." Both officials were said to have been friendly to Japan for many years.

Both, Mr. Chen and Mr. Ling, have been actively co-operating with the Special Service Section of the Japanese Expeditionary Force here in restoring normal conditions in Nantao ever since the evacuation of Chinese troops from the area.

Their first venture was to establish a refugee camp in which 1,500 Chinese were housed and fed.

南市自治委员会

日军占领南市两个月后，南市于昨日下午成立了一个自治委员会，由陈芸先生担任主席。上图显示陈芸先生正在发表就职演说。他左侧是一名将其演讲翻译成日语的译员。仪式在凤来路的一所小学举行，随后委员会官员与日本军官合影留念，如下图所示。[同盟社]

南市成立自治委员会

隆重的就职典礼标志着新行政机构的开启；旨在结束匮乏并 usher in 和平时代

就在日军占领南市整整两个月后，昨日下午1时，华界正式成立了一个自治委员会。

就职典礼庄重甚至隆重，在南市凤来路的私城小学举行。

新的南市管理机构由主席陈芸先生和副主席凌吉坦先生领导，共有13名成员。

陈芸在仪式上宣读的宣言中表示，成立该委员会是为了“结束战争造成的匮乏，帮助和平居民在幸福与繁荣中从事日常事务”。

宣言称，这一新机构将作为“华中地区更光明未来的种子，使人民从……中解放出来……

东方永久和平及其与中国类似机构合作的愿望。

陈芸先生毕业于法学院，曾担任公安局行政科副科长。据报道，他也是当地律师协会的成员。

凌先生曾在日本受教育，被称为“航运巨头”。据说这两位官员多年来一直对日本友好。

自中国军队撤离该地区以来，陈、凌二人一直积极与驻沪日本远征军特务机关合作，以恢复南市的正常秩序。

他们的首要举措是建立了一个收容并供养1500名中国人的难民营。

S.

南市成立

就在日军占领南市两周年之际，昨日下午1时，一个“所谓的自治委员会”在华界凤来路私城小学举行的仪式上正式成立。

该委员会由主席陈芸先生和副主席凌吉坦先生领导。该机构共有13名成员。

陈芸在仪式上宣读的宣言中称，他的“委员会”成立是为了“结束战争造成的匮乏”。

仪式的细节昨日首先通过日本媒体在上海报道。

日本报道称，与该委员会有关的两名中国人，自日军占领该地区以来，一直积极与驻沪日本远征军特务机关合作，以恢复南市的正常秩序。

报道称，他们的首要举措是建立一个难民营。
后来，据说这两人协助日军接管了“雅基诺安全区的行政管理”。

The French Water Works are situated in Nanteao 
about one mile from the boundefy of the French Conces- 
sion but owing to traffic restrictions in force in 
Nantao, a detour has to be made in order to reach the 


Water Works which mekes the journey one of slightly 


more than two miles. Officials of the French Water 


Works are permitted to travel without interference 
between the Concession and the Water Works. With 
the exception of 2,000,000 galls. of water per day 
which the Shanghai Water Works Co. has been supplying 
to the French Concession since over five years, the 
French Water Works is responsible for the whole of 
the French Concession supply, exclusive of that 
supplied by artesian wells. The-main connection from 
the Settlement is located at Hart Road and Avenue 
Foch intersection. _In addition to the main connection 
there are eight connections located along Avenue Foch 
and Avenue Edward VII, which can be used to supply 
water from the Settlement to the French Concession 
or vice versa in case of an emergency, but in such an 
event the supply would have to be restricted to that 
required by absolute necessity. . 

The French Water Works have no protection other 
than that afforded by the presence of a French gunboat 
which is usually berthed alongside the Kiousin Dock 


which adjoins the French Water Works.

After the withdrawal of the Chinese forces 
from the Shanghai area, the Japanese authorities took 
over control of the Kaochongmiao Arsenal and Kiangnan 
Dock at Nantao, and converted the arsenal into a 
depot for military repairs also the smelting of iron 
and copper for the Japanece Military. There are 
some 1,000 Chinese employees under the supervision 
of 200 Japanese employed in this work. The Kiangnan 
Dock is known as the Shipbuilding Yard of the 
Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha Ltd., where some 3,000 Chinese 
artisans are employed supervised by 300 Japanese. 
Apart from the repair of naval vessels and mercantile 
shipping this dock wise undertskes the building of 
small boats. : 

Persons other than Japanese officials’ and 
workers engaged in the two plants are prohibited from 
entering the premises of the arsenal and the ship- 
building yard, nor are they allowed to pass through 
the military zone between Pan Soong Yuen Road and the 
Si Pao Tan, Kaochongmiao, the Lunghua Aerodrome and 
its vicinity and vicinity of Japanese billets. It is 
learned that the residents of Nantao are experiencing 
great inconvenience because of constant change and 


removal of billets by the Japanese garrisons.
